title.zh: 卷八 魏書八 二公孫陶四張傳
title.en: Volume 8: Book of Wei 8 - Biographies of the two Gongsuns, Tao, and the four Zhangs
title.raw: 卷八 魏書八 二公孫陶四張傳 Volume 8: Book of Wei 8 - Biographies of the two Gongsuns, Tao, and the four Zhangs

sentences.zh: 公孙瓚

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚字伯珪，遼西令支人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan, courtesy name Bogui, was a man of Lingzhi in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan, whose courtesy name was Bogui, came from Lingzhi in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 〈令音郎定反。

translations.literal: 〈Ling is read lang-ding fan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈On the reading of 令 (Ling): lang-ding fan.

sentences.zh: 支音其兒反。〉

translations.literal: Zhi is read qi-er fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The syllable zhi is glossed qi-er fan; end of editorial note.〉

sentences.zh: 為郡門下書佐。

translations.literal: He served as a document clerk under the commandery gate.
translations.idiomatic: He held a post as document clerk at the commandery gate.

sentences.zh: 有姿儀，大音聲，侯太守器之，以女妻焉，

translations.literal: He had fine bearing and a loud voice; Prefect Hou thought highly of him and gave him his daughter in marriage,
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself well and spoke in a booming voice; the prefect, Hou, valued him and married his daughter to him,

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：瓚性辯慧，每白事不肯梢入，常總說數曹事，無有忘誤，太守奇其才。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe says: Zan was quick-witted and eloquent; when reporting affairs he would not submit them piecemeal but would always summarize the business of several bureaus at once, never forgetting or erring, and the prefect marveled at his talent.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈According to the Dianlüe, Zan was clever and articulate: when he reported on office business he refused to file it in dribs and drabs, instead summarizing the affairs of several departments in one go without slip or omission, so the prefect was struck by his ability.〉

sentences.zh: 遣詣涿郡盧植讀經。

translations.literal: He was sent to Zhuo commandery to study the classics under Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities sent him to Zhuo commandery to read the classics under Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 後復為郡吏。

translations.literal: Later he again became a commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to duty as a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉太守坐事徵詣廷尉，瓚為御車，身執徒養。

translations.literal: When Prefect Liu was implicated in a matter and summoned to the commandant of justice, Zan drove his carriage for him and personally performed convict labor and menial service.
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Liu was charged, summoned to the capital for the commandant of justice, Zan drove his carriage and himself took on the corvée labor and menial work of a bondservant.

sentences.zh: 及劉徙日南，瓚具米肉，於北芒上祭先人，舉觴祝曰：「昔為人子，今為人臣，當詣日南。

translations.literal: When Liu was banished to Rinan, Zan prepared rice and meat, on Beimang offered sacrifice to his ancestors, raised his cup and prayed, saying, "Formerly I was someone's son; now I am someone's subject; I must go to Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu was sent into exile in Rinan, Zan set out rice and meat, climbed Beimang to sacrifice to the ancestors, lifted his cup, and vowed: "Once I was a son; now I am a subject, bound for Rinan.

sentences.zh: 日南瘴氣，或恐不還，與先人辭於此。

translations.literal: Rinan has miasmal vapors; perhaps I shall not return; I take leave of the ancestors here.
translations.idiomatic: Rinan is thick with pestilential air—I may never come back—so I bid the ancestors farewell here.

sentences.zh: 」再拜慷慨而起，時見者莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: 」He bowed twice, rose in high emotion, and at the time none who saw it failed to sigh with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: 」He bowed twice, rose with a surge of feeling, and every onlooker was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 劉道得赦還。

translations.literal: Liu on the road obtained a pardon and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was pardoned on the way and came home.

sentences.zh: 瓚以孝廉為郎，除遼東屬國長史。

translations.literal: Zan, on the basis of filial and incorrupt, became a gentleman cadet and was appointed chief clerk of the dependent state of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he entered the Lang office and was appointed chief clerk of the dependent state of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 嘗從數十騎出行塞，見鮮卑數百騎，瓚乃退入空亭中，約其從騎曰：「今不沖之，則死盡矣。

translations.literal: Once, leading several dozen horsemen, he went out beyond the frontier and saw several hundred Xianbei riders; Zan then withdrew into an empty post station and urged his followers, saying, "If we do not charge them now, we shall all die.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding out past the border with a few dozen men, he sighted several hundred Xianbei horsemen. Zan pulled back into an abandoned watchpost and told his escort: "If we do not charge, we are dead to a man.

sentences.zh: 」瓚乃自持矛，兩頭施刃，馳出刺胡，殺傷數十人，亦亡其從騎半，遂得免。

translations.literal: 」Zan then himself grasped a spear with blades fitted to both ends, galloped out to stab the barbarians, wounded or killed several dozen men, also lost half his following horsemen, and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: 」He seized a double-edged spear, spurred out, and stabbed into the Hu ranks, killing or wounding dozens; he lost half his men but broke free.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑懲艾，後不敢復入塞。

translations.literal: The Xianbei were chastened and afterward did not dare again to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson sobered the Xianbei, who thereafter stayed out of the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 遷為涿令。

translations.literal: He was transferred and became magistrate of Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 光和中，涼州賊起，發幽州突騎三千人，假瓚都督行事傳，使將之。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era, when bandits rose in Liangzhou, three thousand picked cavalry from Youzhou were mobilized; Zan was given a credential as acting supervisor of affairs and ordered to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghe reign, rebels erupted in Liangzhou; the court drafted three thousand shock cavalry from Youzhou, issued Zan a temporary commission and tally, and put the detachment under his command.

sentences.zh: 軍到薊中，漁陽張純誘遼西烏丸丘力居等叛，劫略薊中，自號將軍，

translations.literal: When the army reached Ji, Zhang Chun of Yuyang enticed the Wuhuan of western Liaoxi, Qiu Liju and others, to rebel, plundering the Ji region and styling himself general,
translations.idiomatic: The column reached Ji, where Zhang Chun of Yuyang incited the western Liaoxi Wuhuan under Qiu Liju to rise, raid the Ji area, and proclaim himself general,

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：純自號彌天將軍、安定王。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou Chunqiu says: Chun styled himself General Who Fills Heaven and King of Anding.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiuzhou Chunqiu records that Chun called himself the "Heaven-filling" general and king of Anding.〉

sentences.zh: 略吏民攻右北平、遼西屬國諸城，所至殘破。

translations.literal: He plundered officials and people and attacked the cities of Youbeiping and the dependent state of western Liaoxi; wherever he went he left ruin.
translations.idiomatic: His bands looted townsfolk, stormed Youbeiping and the western Liaoxi dependent state, and left a trail of destruction.

sentences.zh: 瓚將所領，追討純等有功，遷騎都尉。

translations.literal: Zan, leading the troops under his command, pursued and attacked Chun and others with merit, and was promoted to chief of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zan led his own troops in the pursuit, distinguished himself, and was raised to chief of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 屬國烏丸貪至王率種人詣瓚降。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan king Tan Zhi of the dependent state led his people to Zan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhi, Wuhuan king of the dependent state, brought his tribesmen in submission to Zan.

sentences.zh: 遷中郎將，封都亭侯，進屯屬國，與胡相攻擊五六年。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general of the gentlemen of the household, enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct, advanced to garrison the dependent state, and with the Hu fought each other off and on for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the gentlemen of the household, was enfeoffed village marquis at the metropolitan gate, pushed his camp into the dependent state, and skirmished with the Hu for five or six years.

sentences.zh: 丘力居等鈔略青、徐、幽、冀，四州被其害，瓚不能禦。

translations.literal: Qiu Liju and others raided Qing, Xu, You, and Ji; the four provinces suffered their harm, and Zan could not check them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Liju and company harried Qing, Xu, You, and Ji, and Zan proved unable to stop them.

sentences.zh: 朝議以宗正東海劉伯安既有德義，昔為幽州刺史，恩信流著，戎狄附之，若使鎮撫，可不勞眾而定，乃以劉虞為幽州牧。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that Liu Boan the director of the imperial clan, prince of Donghai, had both virtue and righteousness, had formerly been governor of Youzhou, and his grace and trust had spread abroad so that the Rong and Di attached to him; if he were sent to pacify and console, it could be settled without troubling the host, and therefore Liu Yu was made governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Liu Boan of the imperial house, prince of Donghai—virtuous, once governor of Youzhou, and still remembered for winning the allegiance of frontier peoples—could restore order without a major campaign, and appointed Liu Yu as governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：虞，東海恭王之後也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: Yu was a descendant of Prince Gong of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu states that Yu descended from Prince Gong of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 遭世衰亂，又與時主疏遠，仕縣為戶曹吏。

translations.literal: Encountering a generation of decline and chaos, and also being distant from the ruler of the time, he served in the county as clerk for households.
translations.idiomatic: He came of age in turmoil and had little access to power, so he began as a county clerk for household registers.

sentences.zh: 以能治身奉職，召為郡吏，以孝廉為郎，累遷至幽州刺史，轉甘陵相，甚得東土戎狄之心。

translations.literal: Because he could cultivate himself and perform his duties, he was summoned as a commandery clerk; on the basis of filial and incorrupt he became a gentleman cadet, and by successive promotions reached governor of Youzhou, then transferred to be chancellor of Ganling, and greatly won the hearts of the eastern lands and the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: His self-discipline and conscientious service won him a commandery post; as a filial-and-incorrupt appointee he entered the Lang office, climbed to governor of Youzhou, then became chancellor of Ganling, earning deep goodwill across the east and among the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 後以疾歸家，常降身隱約，與邑黨州閭同樂共卹，等齊有無，不以名位自殊，鄉曲咸共宗之。

translations.literal: Later, because of illness he returned home, always lowering himself and living modestly, sharing joy and grief with his township and neighborhood, evening out plenty and want, not distinguishing himself by name or rank, and the countryside all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Illness sent him home, where he lived modestly among neighbors, sharing weal and woe and pooling resources without pulling rank, until local society looked to him as a moral anchor.

sentences.zh: 時鄉曲有所訴訟，不以詣吏，自投虞平之；

translations.literal: When the countryside had lawsuits, they did not go to the clerks but submitted themselves to Yu for him to settle them;
translations.idiomatic: Villagers with disputes bypassed the yamen and brought their cases straight to Yu;

sentences.zh: 虞以情理為之論判，皆大小敬從，不以為恨。

translations.literal: Yu judged them by reason and sentiment, and all, great and small, respectfully obeyed and did not harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: he settled each on its merits, and parties great and small accepted his verdicts without bitterness.

sentences.zh: 嘗有失牛者，骨體毛色，與虞牛相似，因以為是，虞便推與之；

translations.literal: Once there was one who had lost an ox; its bones, frame, and coat color resembled Yu's ox, and therefore he thought it was his, and Yu immediately yielded it to him;
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor once mistook Yu's ox for his own—the build and hide matched—and Yu handed the animal over without argument;

sentences.zh: 後主自得本牛，乃還謝罪。

translations.literal: later the owner recovered his own ox and then returned to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: when the man recovered his beast, he came back ashamed to make amends.

sentences.zh: 會甘陵复亂，吏民思虞治行，復以為甘陵相，甘陵大治。

translations.literal: When Ganling again rebelled, officials and people longed for Yu's administration and again made him chancellor of Ganling, and Ganling was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Ganling erupted anew; the populace wanted Yu back, reinstalled him as chancellor, and the district flourished under his hand.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書令、光祿勳，以公族有禮，更為宗正。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed supervisor of the masters of writing and superintendent of the household for the shining horses; because as a member of the ducal house he observed ritual, he was further made director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court as supervisor of the masters of writing and shining-household superintendent, he was soon named director of the imperial clan in recognition of his ritual propriety as a kinsman of the throne.

sentences.zh: 《英雄記》曰：虞為博平令，治正推平，高尚純樸，境內無盜賊，災害不生。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: When Yu was magistrate of Boping, his government was upright and even, lofty and plain, and within his borders there were no bandits and calamities did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji records that as magistrate of Boping he ruled evenhandedly and lived simply, so that banditry vanished and misfortune rarely touched the district.

sentences.zh: 時鄰縣接壤，蝗蟲為害，至博平界，飛過不入。

translations.literal: At the time neighboring counties bordered him; locusts did harm, but reaching the border of Boping they flew past and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged adjoining counties yet swerved around Boping's line as if repelled.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》曰：虞在幽州，清靜儉約，以禮義化民。

translations.literal: The Weishu says: In Youzhou Yu was quiet, frugal, and restrained, transforming the people with ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The Weishu adds that in Youzhou he kept government spare and frugal, shaping custom through rite and duty.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，南宮災，吏遷補州郡者，皆責助治宮錢，或一千萬，或二千萬，富者以私財辨，或發民錢以備之，貧而清慎者，無以充調，或至自殺。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ling's time, when the southern palace burned, those officials transferred to fill posts in provinces and commanderies were all assessed a levy to repair the palace, some ten million or twenty million cash; the rich used private wealth to meet it, or the people's money was raised to supply it, while the poor who were scrupulous had no means to meet the levy and some even killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling, after the southern palace fire, newly posted provincial officials were forced to "contribute" toward rebuilding—sums of ten or twenty million; the rich bought their way clear, commoners were squeezed, and honest poor men, unable to pay, took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 靈帝以虞清貧，特不使出錢。〉

translations.literal: Emperor Ling, because Yu was poor and pure, specially ordered that he not be required to pay out money.〉
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exempted Yu alone, knowing he was clean-handed and destitute.〉

sentences.zh: 虞到，遣使至胡中，告以利害，責使送純首。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, he sent envoys into the Hu lands, informing them of benefit and harm and charging them to deliver Chun's head.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reached his post, sent envoys among the Hu to explain costs and gains, and demanded Zhang Chun's head.

sentences.zh: 丘力居等聞虞至，喜，各遣譯自歸。

translations.literal: When Qiu Liju and others heard Yu had come, they rejoiced and each sent interpreters to submit of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Liju and the rest welcomed Yu's arrival and each dispatched interpreters to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 瓚害虞有功，乃陰使人徼殺胡使。

translations.literal: Zan, jealous that Yu had merit, secretly sent men to intercept and kill the Hu envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, resentful of Yu's success, secretly had the Hu messengers waylaid and murdered.

sentences.zh: 胡知其情，間行詣虞。

translations.literal: The Hu learned the truth and by secret routes went to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu discovered the plot and stole through bypaths to reach Yu.

sentences.zh: 虞上罷諸屯兵，但留瓚將步騎萬人屯右北平。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized to dismiss the various garrison troops but to leave Zan leading ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Youbeiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked the throne to stand down the scattered garrisons while keeping Zan with ten thousand foot and horse at Youbeiping.

sentences.zh: 純乃棄妻子，逃入鮮卑，為其客王政所殺，送首詣虞。

translations.literal: Chun then abandoned wife and children, fled into the Xianbei, and was killed by his retainer Wang Zheng, who sent the head to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun abandoned his family, fled to the Xianbei, and was slain by his client Wang Zheng, who delivered the head to Yu.

sentences.zh: 封政為列侯。

translations.literal: Zheng was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zheng received a full marquisate for the deed.

sentences.zh: 虞以功即拜太尉，封襄賁侯。

translations.literal: Yu, on account of merit, was immediately appointed grand commandant and enfeoffed marquis of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: For these services Yu was named grand commandant at once and enfeoffed marquis of Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：虞讓太尉，因薦衛尉趙謨、益州牧劉焉、豫州牧黃琬、南陽太守羊續，並任為公。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Yu declined the grand commandantship and recommended Commandant of the guards Zhao Mo, Governor of Yizhou Liu Yan, Governor of Yuzhou Huang Wan, and Governor of Nanyang Yang Xu, all to serve as dukes.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji notes that Yu tried to refuse the grand commandantship and nominated Zhao Mo, Liu Yan, Huang Wan, and Yang Xu for exalted posts.〉

sentences.zh: 會董卓至洛陽，遷虞大司馬，瓚奮武將軍，封薊侯。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo reached Luoyang, Yu was transferred to grand marshal and Zan to general who displays might, enfeoffed marquis of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's entry into Luoyang brought Yu promotion to grand marshal and Zan to general who displays might, with a marquisate at Ji.

sentences.zh: 關東義兵起，卓遂劫帝西遷，徵虞為太傅，道路隔塞，信命不得至。

translations.literal: When the righteous armies of east of the pass rose, Zhuo then seized the emperor and moved west, summoning Yu as grand tutor, but the roads were blocked and sealed and orders could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: As the eastern coalition rose, Zhuo dragged the court west and named Yu grand tutor, but couriers could not get through the cut lines.

sentences.zh: 袁紹、韓馥議，以為少帝制於奸臣，天下無所歸心。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao and Han Fu deliberated, holding that the young emperor was controlled by treacherous ministers and the empire had nowhere to fix its loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Han Fu argued that the boy emperor was a puppet and the realm lacked a rallying point.

sentences.zh: 虞，宗室知名，民之望也，遂推虞為帝。

translations.literal: Yu, of the imperial house and renowned, was the people's hope, and therefore they pushed Yu to be emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They cast Liu Yu of the imperial house—the people's hope—as the man to mount the throne.

sentences.zh: 遣使詣虞，虞終不肯受。

translations.literal: They sent envoys to Yu, but Yu in the end was unwilling to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys pressed the offer; Yu steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 紹等復勸虞領尚書事，承製封拜，虞又不聽，然猶與紹等連和。

translations.literal: Shao and others again urged Yu to take charge of the masters of writing and, by interim authority, to issue enfeoffments and appointments, but Yu again would not listen, yet still kept alliance with Shao and others.
translations.idiomatic: They asked him to head the secretariat and issue orders in the emperor's name; he declined again yet stayed in coalition with them.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：紹、馥使故樂浪太守甘陵張岐齎議詣虞，使即尊號。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiuzhou Chunqiu says: Shao and Fu sent the former governor of Lelang, Zhang Qi of Ganling, bearing their proposal to Yu, urging him to assume the supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiuzhou Chunqiu: Shao and Han Fu dispatched former Lelang governor Zhang Qi of Ganling with a petition urging Yu to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 虞厲聲呵岐曰：「卿敢出此言乎！

translations.literal: Yu sternly rebuked Qi, saying, "How dare you speak such words!
translations.idiomatic: Yu thundered at Zhang Qi: "How dare you utter this!

sentences.zh: 忠孝之道，既不能濟。

translations.literal: The way of loyalty and filial piety, you have been unable to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot even uphold loyalty and filial duty yourselves.

sentences.zh: 孤受國恩，天下擾亂，未能竭命以除國恥，望諸州郡烈義之士戮力西面，援迎幼主，而乃妄造逆謀，欲塗污忠臣邪！

translations.literal: I alone have received the state's grace; the empire is in turmoil and I have been unable to exhaust my life to wipe away the national shame; I look to the righteous men of the provinces and commanderies to join strength toward the west, rescue and welcome the young ruler—and you want recklessly to devise treasonous plots and smear loyal ministers!
translations.idiomatic: I owe the dynasty everything, yet I have not spent myself to avenge its shame. I count on every loyal commandery westward to rally, escort the boy sovereign back—and you invent sedition to drag good officials through the mud!

sentences.zh: 」《吳書》曰：馥以書與袁術，云帝非孝靈子，欲依絳、灌誅廢少主，迎立代王故事；

translations.literal: 」The Wushu says: Fu wrote to Yuan Shu saying the emperor was not the son of Emperor Xiaoling and wished to follow the old story of Zhou Bo and Guan Ying in executing and deposing the young lord and welcoming the prince of Dai to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: 」The Wushu adds that Han Fu wrote Yuan Shu claiming the emperor was no son of Ling, proposing a Zhou Bo–style purge of the puppet and enthronement of a princely heir,

sentences.zh: 稱虞功德治行，華夏少二，當今公室枝屬，皆莫能及。

translations.literal: praising Yu's merit, virtue, and administration, saying that within the Huaxia there was scarcely a second, and that among the collateral branches of the ducal house today none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: praising Yu's record as unmatched among imperial cadres and the Liu kin.

sentences.zh: 又云：「昔光武去定王五世，以大司馬領河北，耿弇、馮異勸即尊號，卒代更始。

translations.literal: It also said: "Formerly Guangwu was five generations removed from the prince of Ding; as grand marshal commanding Hebei, Geng Yan and Feng Yi urged him to assume the supreme title, and in the end he replaced Gengshi.
translations.idiomatic: The letter cited Guangwu, five generations from the prince of Ding, who as Hebei grand marshal took the throne on Geng Yan and Feng Yi's urging and supplanted Gengshi,

sentences.zh: 今劉公自恭王枝別，其數亦五，以大司馬領幽州牧，此其與光武同。

translations.literal: Now Lord Liu branches from Prince Gong as the fifth generation as well; as grand marshal he holds the governorship of Youzhou—this matches Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: and argued that Liu Yu, likewise five generations from Prince Gong and grand marshal of Youzhou, mirrored that precedent.

sentences.zh: 」是時有四星會於箕尾，馥稱讖云神人將在燕分。

translations.literal: 」At this time four stars gathered in Ji and Wei; Fu cited a prophecy that a divine man would arise in the Yan region.
translations.idiomatic: 」Han Fu also cited omens: four stars clustered over Ji-Wei, a prophecy of a sage in the Yan quarter.

sentences.zh: 又言濟陰男子王定得玉印，文曰「虞為天子」。

translations.literal: It also said that the man Wang Ding of Jiyin obtained a jade seal inscribed "Yu shall be Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He mentioned a peasant of Jiyin who found a jade seal reading "Yu for Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 又見兩日出於代郡，謂虞當代立。

translations.literal: It also said that two suns appeared over Dai commandery, meaning Yu should replace the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of twin suns over Dai commandery as a sign Yu would succeed the Han.

sentences.zh: 紹又別書報術。

translations.literal: Shao also separately sent a letter reporting to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent a parallel letter to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 是時術陰有不臣之心，不利國家有長主，外託公義以答拒之。

translations.literal: At this time Shu secretly harbored a disloyal heart and did not desire that the state have a mature ruler; outwardly he pleaded public righteousness in answering and refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, already nursing ambition, disliked a grown emperor on the throne and masked refusal in language of public duty.

sentences.zh: 紹亦使人私報虞，虞以國有正統，非人臣所宜言，固辭不許；

translations.literal: Shao also sent someone privately to report to Yu; Yu, because the state had a legitimate succession, held that it was not what a subject should speak of, firmly declined and would not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Shao also sounded Yu privately; Yu replied that a legitimate line still sat on the throne and such talk ill befitted a minister,

sentences.zh: 乃欲圖奔匈奴以自絕，紹等乃止。

translations.literal: then wished to flee to the Xiongnu to cut himself off, and Shao and others then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: then threatened flight to the Xiongnu to break with the plotters, at which they desisted.

sentences.zh: 虞於是奉職脩貢，愈益恭肅；

translations.literal: Yu thereupon performed his duties and repaired tribute, ever more respectful and solemn;
translations.idiomatic: Yu thereafter kept sending tribute and memorials in scrupulous loyalty,

sentences.zh: 諸外國羌、胡有所貢獻，道路不通，皆為傳送，致之京師。〉

translations.literal: whatever the foreign Qiang and Hu offered as tribute, when the roads were impassable, he had it all relayed and delivered to the capital.〉
translations.idiomatic: and whenever Qiang or Hu gifts could not reach Luoyang, he relayed them eastward himself.〉

sentences.zh: 虞子和為侍中，在長安。

translations.literal: Yu's son Liu He was attendant at the palace and was in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu He served as palace attendant in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天子思東歸，使和偽逃卓，潛出武關詣虞，令將兵來迎。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven longed to return east and ordered He feign escape from Zhuo, secretly to leave through Wu Pass and go to Yu, ordering him to bring troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, desperate to return east, told He to slip Zhuo's guard, steal out by Wu Pass to Yu, and bid him march an escort.

sentences.zh: 和道經袁術，為說天子意。

translations.literal: He on the road passed Yuan Shu and explained to him the Son of Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Yuan Shu's path and explained the sovereign's plea.

sentences.zh: 術利虞為援，留和不遣，許兵至俱西，令和為書與虞。

translations.literal: Shu, profiting from Yu as a support, detained He and would not send him, promising that when troops arrived they would go west together, and ordered He to write a letter to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, coveting Yu as an ally, held He hostage, promised a joint advance west once troops gathered, and made him write to his father.

sentences.zh: 虞得和書，乃遣數千騎詣和。

translations.literal: When Yu received He's letter, he then sent several thousand riders to He.
translations.idiomatic: Yu read the letter and dispatched several thousand horsemen toward his son.

sentences.zh: 瓚知術有異志，不欲遣兵，止虞，虞不可。

translations.literal: Zan knew Shu had a different intent and did not wish to send troops; he stopped Yu, but Yu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zan saw Shu's duplicity and tried to block the expedition; Yu overruled him.

sentences.zh: 瓚懼術聞而怨之，亦遣其從弟越將千騎詣術以自結，而陰教術執和，奪其兵。

translations.literal: Zan feared that if Shu heard he would resent him; he also sent his cousin Yue leading a thousand riders to Shu to cement ties, while secretly instructing Shu to seize He and seize his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shu's spite, Zan also sent his cousin Yue with a thousand riders to court Shu while secretly telling Shu to arrest He and seize the column.

sentences.zh: 由是虞、瓚益有隙。

translations.literal: From this Yu and Zan increasingly had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: The two allies were now openly at odds.

sentences.zh: 和逃術來北，復為紹所留。

translations.literal: He fled Shu and came north, and again was detained by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He broke away northward only to be held again by Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 是時，術遣孫堅屯陽城拒卓，紹使周昂奪其處。

translations.literal: At this time Shu sent Sun Jian to garrison Yangcheng to resist Zhuo; Shao ordered Zhou Ang to seize his position.
translations.idiomatic: Shu stationed Sun Jian at Yangcheng against Dong Zhuo; Shao sent Zhou Ang to oust him.

sentences.zh: 術遣越與堅攻昂，不勝，越為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: Shu sent Yue with Jian to attack Ang; they did not prevail, and Yue was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yue joined Sun Jian against Zhou Ang, failed, and fell to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 瓚怒曰：「余弟死，禍起於紹。

translations.literal: Zan angrily said, "My younger brother died; the disaster arose from Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Zan roared, "My cousin is dead—and Shao caused it.

sentences.zh: 」遂出軍屯磐河，將以報紹。

translations.literal: 」He then led the army out and garrisoned at the Pan River, intending thereby to repay Shao.
translations.idiomatic: 」He marched the host to the Pan River to settle scores with Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹懼，以所佩勃海太守印綬授瓚從弟範，遣之郡，欲以結援。

translations.literal: Shao feared him and gave the seal and ribbon of the Bohai governorship that he wore at his belt to Zan's cousin Fan, sending him to the commandery, wishing thereby to cement support.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, alarmed, handed his Bohai seal-ribbon to Zan's cousin Fan and sent him to that seat to buy goodwill.

sentences.zh: 範遂以勃海兵助瓚，破青、徐黃巾，兵益盛；

translations.literal: Fan then used Bohai troops to assist Zan, broke the Qing and Xu Yellow Turbans, and his troops grew stronger;
translations.idiomatic: Fan brought Bohai levies to Zan's side, shattered the Qing–Xu Yellow Turbans, and swelled their strength,

sentences.zh: 進軍界橋。

translations.literal: and advanced the army to Jie Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: then drove the line to Jie Bridge.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》載瓚表紹罪狀曰：〉

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe records Zan's memorial listing Shao's crimes, saying:〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Dianlüe preserves Zan's indictment of Shao, which begins:〉

sentences.zh: 臣聞皇、羲以來，始有君臣上下之事，張化以導民，刑罰以禁暴。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that from Huang and Xi onward there began to be the affairs of ruler and subject, high and low; they spread transformation to guide the people and punishments to forbid violence.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that since the sage-kings Huang and Xi there have been rulers and subjects, instruction to guide the people, and penal law to curb violence.

sentences.zh: 今行車騎將軍袁紹，託其先軌，寇竊人爵，既性暴亂，厥行淫穢。

translations.literal: Now the general of chariots and cavalry Yuan Shao, relying on his ancestors' tracks, usurped others' noble ranks; moreover his nature is violent and chaotic and his conduct lewd and foul.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chariot-and-cavalry general Yuan Shao, trading on pedigree, stole honors; he is by nature cruel and depraved.

sentences.zh: 昔為司隸校尉，會值國家喪禍之際，太后承攝，何氏輔政，紹專為邪媚，不能舉直，至令丁原焚燒孟津，招來董卓，造為亂根，紹罪一也。

translations.literal: Formerly, as colonel director of retainers, he met the time when the state met with the disaster of mourning; the empress dowager held the regency and the He clan assisted in government, and Shao devoted himself to wicked flattery and could not uphold the straight; to the extent that Ding Yuan burned Meng Ford and summoned Dong Zhuo, creating the root of chaos—this is Shao's first crime.
translations.idiomatic: As colonel director of retainers during the He regency he flattered the powerful, failed to speak truth, let Ding Yuan torch Meng Ford and invite Dong Zhuo—crime the first.

sentences.zh: 卓既入雒而主見質，紹不能權譎以濟君父，而棄置節傳，迸竄逃亡，忝辱爵命，背上不忠，紹罪二也。

translations.literal: When Zhuo had entered Luo and the ruler was held hostage, Shao could not use stratagem to rescue lord and father but cast aside his credentials and fled in panic, disgracing his noble commission, turning his back on the sovereign—disloyalty above—this is Shao's second crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo seized Luoyang and the emperor, Shao bolted, abandoning his charge—crime the second.

sentences.zh: 紹為勃海太守，默選戎馬，當攻董卓，不告父兄，至使太傅門戶，太僕母子，一旦而斃，不仁不孝，紹罪三也。

translations.literal: Shao, as governor of Bohai, secretly selected war horses; when he should have attacked Dong Zhuo he did not inform father or elder brothers, with the result that the gates of the grand tutor, the households of the grand coachman, mother and son, in one morning perished—unkind and unfilial—this is Shao's third crime.
translations.idiomatic: As Bohai governor he armed in secret, struck Zhuo without warning his kin, and brought death on the grand tutor's household—crime the third.

sentences.zh: 紹既興兵，涉歷二年，不恤國難，廣自封殖，乃多以資糧專為不急，割剝富室，收考責錢，百姓吁嗟，莫不痛怨，紹罪四也。

translations.literal: Shao, having raised troops, passed through two years, did not pity the state's difficulties, broadly enriched himself, and moreover used much grain and supplies for what was not urgent, carved and stripped the rich houses, seized and extorted cash; the hundred surnames groaned and none did not bitterly resent—this is Shao's fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Two years of war enriched him while the realm starved; he mulcted the wealthy and wrung the commons—crime the fourth.

sentences.zh: 韓馥之迫，竊其虛位，矯命詔恩，刻金印玉璽，每下文書，皁囊施檢，文曰『詔書一封，邟鄉侯印』。

translations.literal: Han Fu's being pressured, he stole his empty position, forged edicts of grace, carved gold seals and jade seals, and whenever he issued documents below, black pouches with seals were applied, the text reading "Imperial rescript, one bundle, seal of the marquis of Xiangxiang."
translations.idiomatic: He hijacked Han Fu's seat, forged rescripts, minted gold seals and jade tallies, and dispatched black-silk packets stamped "Imperial edict—one—Marquis of Xiangxiang."

sentences.zh: 邟，口浪反。

translations.literal: Xiang is read kou-lang fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character rendered Xiang in the text is glossed kou-lang fan.

sentences.zh: 昔新室之亂，漸以即真，今紹所施，擬而方之，紹罪五也。

translations.literal: Formerly in the turmoil of the Xin dynasty they gradually advanced toward taking true title; what Shao now practices may be compared and matched to it—this is Shao's fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's Xin seizure of power crept toward the throne in stages; Shao's schemes replay that pattern—count five in the indictment.

sentences.zh: 紹令崔巨業候視星日，財貨賂遺，與共飲食，剋期會合，攻鈔郡縣，此豈大臣所當宜為？

translations.literal: Shao ordered Cui Juye to watch the stars and days, with goods and wealth as bribes and gifts, sharing drink and food, fixing a date to join forces, attacking and plundering commanderies and counties—is this what a great minister ought properly to do?
translations.idiomatic: He set Cui Juye to read the omens, bought allies with feasts and silver, fixed a day to strike, then looted county seats—hardly the conduct of a senior statesman.

sentences.zh: 紹罪六也。

translations.literal: Shao's sixth crime.
translations.idiomatic: That is his sixth offense.

sentences.zh: 紹與故虎牙都尉劉勛首共造兵，勳仍有效，又降伏張楊，而以小忿枉害於勳，信用讒慝，殺害有功，紹罪七也。

translations.literal: Shao together with the former colonel of tiger fangs Liu Xun first jointly raised troops; Xun still had merit, also subdued Zhang Yang, yet because of a small resentment wrongly harmed Xun, trusted slanderers, and killed the meritorious—Shao's seventh crime.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Xun of the Tiger Fang guard first raised an army; Xun had real achievements and had forced Zhang Yang to yield, yet Shao murdered him over a trifle, heeding malice and destroying a proven captain—crime seven.

sentences.zh: 紹又上故上谷太守高焉、故甘陵相姚貢，橫責其錢，錢不備畢，二人並命，紹罪八也。

translations.literal: Shao further impeached the former governor of Shanggu Gao Yan and the former chancellor of Ganling Yao Gong, extorting their money; when the money was not fully collected, both lost their lives—Shao's eighth crime.
translations.idiomatic: He hounded two retired officials for cash until they could not pay and died—crime eight.

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，子以母貴。

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn is: the son is honored through the mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Chunqiu rule runs: a son's rank follows his mother's standing.

sentences.zh: 紹母親為婢使，紹實微賤，不可以為人後，以義不宜，乃據豐隆之重任，忝污王爵，損辱袁宗，紹罪九也。

translations.literal: Shao's birth mother had been a bondmaid; Shao was in truth base and low and could not be made another's heir; by righteousness it was not fitting, yet he seized the heavy charge of Feng and Long, disgracing the royal title and shaming the Yuan house—Shao's ninth crime.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a servant girl, so by ritual he lacked stature to inherit exalted line, yet he grasped the high command of Feng and Long, sullying the ducal fief and the Yuan clan—crime nine.

sentences.zh: 又長沙太守孫堅，前領豫州刺史，驅走董卓，掃除陵廟，其功莫大；

translations.literal: Moreover the governor of Changsha Sun Jian, formerly acting governor of Yuzhou, drove off Dong Zhuo and cleansed the imperial shrines—his merit was without peer;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian of Changsha, once acting governor of Yuzhou, expelled Dong Zhuo and purged the tombs—no one's service matched his;

sentences.zh: 紹令周昂盜居其位，斷絕堅糧，令不得入，使卓不被誅，紹罪十也。

translations.literal: Shao ordered Zhou Ang thievishly to occupy his post, cut off Jian's grain, made him unable to advance, so that Zhuo was not executed—Shao's tenth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shao set Zhou Ang to usurp his command, starve his column, and block his advance, leaving Zhuo alive—crime ten.

sentences.zh: 臣又每得後將軍袁術書，云紹非術類也。

translations.literal: Your subject moreover repeatedly received letters from General of the Rear Yuan Shu saying Shao was not of Shu's kind.
translations.idiomatic: Letters from General of the Rear Yuan Shu repeatedly insist Shao is no true kinsman of his.

sentences.zh: 紹之罪戾，雖南山之竹不能載。

translations.literal: Shao's crimes and guilt, even bamboo south of the mountain could not bear recording them.
translations.idiomatic: Not every bamboo grove south of the Qin range could hold the scroll of his misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 昔姬周政弱，王道陵遲，天子遷都，諸侯背叛，於是齊桓立柯亭之，晉文為踐土之會，伐荊楚以致菁茅，誅曹、衛以彰無禮。

translations.literal: Formerly the house of Ji and Zhou grew weak, the kingly way declined and delayed, the Son of Heaven moved the capital, the feudal lords turned their backs; thereupon Duke Huan of Qi set up the covenant at Ke, Duke Wen of Jin held the meeting at Jiantu, attacked Jing and Chu to demand the green sedge, executed Cao and Wei to display their lack of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When royal Zhou faltered and vassals broke faith, Qi Huan swore the Ke pact and Jin Wen convened at Jiantu, chastised Chu for tribute and struck Cao and Wei for impiety.

sentences.zh: 臣雖闒茸，名非先賢，蒙被朝恩，當此重任，職在鈇鉞，奉辭伐罪，輒與諸將州郡兵討紹等。

translations.literal: Your subject though mean and lowly, my name not that of former worthies, have received court grace and hold this heavy responsibility; my office lies in axe and halberd; receiving mandate to punish crime, I therefore together with the generals and commandery troops attack Shao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am no sage, I bear the court's axe of execution and shall join every column in the field against Shao.

sentences.zh: 若事克捷，罪人斯得，庶續桓、文忠誠之效，攻戰形狀，前後續上。

translations.literal: If the affair succeeds and the criminals are seized, perhaps continuing the loyal effect of Huan and Wen; the forms of battle before and after shall be reported in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Should we prevail and lay hands on the culprits, we may match the steadfast service of Huan and Wen; dispatches on the fighting will follow in order.

sentences.zh: 〈遂舉兵與紹對戰，紹不勝。〉

translations.literal: 〈Thereupon he raised troops and fought Shao in opposition; Shao did not prevail.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈He then took the field against Shao and got the better of him.〉

sentences.zh: 以嚴綱為冀州，田楷為青州，單經為兗州，置諸郡縣。

translations.literal: He appointed Yan Gang over Jizhou, Tian Kai over Qingzhou, Dan Jing over Yanzhou, and established the various commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yan Gang for Ji, Tian Kai for Qing, Dan Jing for Yan, and parcelled out county seats under them.

sentences.zh: 紹軍廣川，令將麴義先登與瓚戰，生禽綱。

translations.literal: Shao's army was at Guangchuan; he ordered the general Qu Yi to lead the van to fight Zan and captured Gang alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shao held Guangchuan and sent Qu Yi's van against Zan; they took Yan Gang, whom Zan had posted there, prisoner.

sentences.zh: 瓚軍敗走勃海，與範俱還薊，於大城東南築小城，與虞相近，稍相恨望。

translations.literal: Zan's army was defeated and fled toward Bohai; together with Fan both returned to Ji, southeast of the great rampart built a small fort, close to Yu, and gradually nursed mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's line broke toward Bohai, then he and Fan withdrew into Ji, raised a satellite citadel southeast of the main walls next to Yu's camp, and the two allies slid into open enmity.

sentences.zh: 虞懼瓚為變，遂舉兵襲瓚。

translations.literal: Yu feared Zan would make a coup, thereupon raised troops to surprise Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, fearing a coup, struck first at Zan.

sentences.zh: 虞為瓚所敗，出奔居庸。

translations.literal: Yu was defeated by Zan, fled out toward Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zan broke him and drove him toward Juyong pass.

sentences.zh: 瓚攻拔居庸，生獲虞，執虞還薊。

translations.literal: Zan attacked and took Juyong, captured Yu alive, seized Yu and returned to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zan stormed Juyong, took Yu prisoner, and marched him back to Ji.

sentences.zh: 會卓死，天子遣使者段訓增虞邑，督六州；

translations.literal: When Zhuo died, the Son of Heaven sent the envoy Duan Xun to enlarge Yu's fief and supervise six provinces;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuo fell, the court sent Duan Xun to swell Yu's estate and give him oversight of six provinces;

sentences.zh: 瓚遷前將軍，封易侯。

translations.literal: Zan was promoted general of the van and enfeoffed marquis of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was raised to general of the van and enfeoffed marquis of Yi.

sentences.zh: 瓚誣虞欲稱尊號，脅訓斬虞。

translations.literal: Zan falsely accused Yu of intending to assume the supreme title, coerced Xun, and beheaded Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered Yu as a pretender, forced Xun's compliance, and had Yu executed.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：初，劉虞和輯戎狄，瓚以胡夷難禦，當因不賓而討之，今加財賞，必益輕漢，效一時之名，非久長深慮。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei shi Chunqiu says: At first, when Liu Yu harmonized and gathered the Rong and Di, Zan held that the Hu and Yi were hard to control and ought to be attacked when unsubmissive; now if wealth and rewards are added, they will surely slight the Han all the more, seeking a moment's fame, not a long-term deep plan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Annals notes: Yu wished to win the frontier peoples by kindness; Zan argued they were untamable and should be beaten when defiant, and that bribes would only teach them to despise the court for short-term gain.

sentences.zh: 故虞所賞賜，瓚輒鈔奪。

translations.literal: Therefore whatever Yu rewarded and bestowed, Zan always plundered and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Yu gave them, Zan intercepted.

sentences.zh: 虞數請會，稱疾不往。

translations.literal: Yu several times requested meetings; he claimed illness and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Yu summoned him repeatedly; Zan pleaded sickness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 至是戰敗，虞欲討之，告東曹掾右北平人魏攸。

translations.literal: When he had been defeated in battle, Yu wished to attack him and informed the eastern-department aide Wei You of Youbeiping.
translations.idiomatic: After that reverse Yu resolved to destroy him and took counsel with Wei You of Youbeiping.

sentences.zh: 攸曰：「今天下引領，以公為歸，謀臣爪牙，不可無也。

translations.literal: You said: "Now the empire cranes its neck, taking you, lord, as its refuge; plotting ministers and claws and teeth cannot be dispensed with.
translations.idiomatic: You replied: "The realm looks to you; you still need sharp swords at your side.

sentences.zh: 瓚，文武才力足恃，雖有小惡，固宜容忍。

translations.literal: Zan, in civil and military talent and strength, is sufficient to rely on; though he has small faults, solidly he ought to be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Zan is able in civil and military affairs; overlook his lesser vices."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: 」Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yu dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 後一年，攸病死。

translations.literal: After a year You died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Wei You died.

sentences.zh: 虞又與官屬議，密令眾襲瓚。

translations.literal: Yu again deliberated with his officials and secretly ordered the host to raid Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu met his staff again and ordered a secret strike on Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚部曲放散在外，自懼敗，掘東城門欲走。

translations.literal: Zan's troops were scattered abroad; he himself feared defeat and dug at the east gate intending to flee.
translations.idiomatic: With his units still in the field, Zan saw the assault failing and tried to cut his way out through the east gate.

sentences.zh: 虞兵無部伍，不習戰，又愛民屋，敕令勿燒。

translations.literal: Yu's troops had no battle order, were unpracticed in war, also cherished the people's houses, and ordered them not to set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's men were green, ill-drilled, and he forbade torching homes for fear of the populace.

sentences.zh: 故瓚得放火，因以精銳衝突。

translations.literal: Therefore Zan was able to set fires and with picked troops charge through.
translations.idiomatic: Zan burned freely and drove elite horse through the gap.

sentences.zh: 虞眾大潰，奔居庸城。

translations.literal: Yu's host was utterly routed and fled to Juyong town.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's army collapsed and ran for the walls of Juyong.

sentences.zh: 瓚攻及家屬以還，殺害州府，衣冠善士殆盡。

translations.literal: Zan's attack overtook family members on the return, killed and harmed the province and prefecture, and caps-and-gowns good scholars were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On the retreat Zan cut down Yu's kin, slaughtered provincial officers, and all but wiped out the gentry of the yamen.

sentences.zh: 《典略》曰：瓚曝虞於市而祝曰：「若應為天子者，天當降雨救之。

translations.literal: The Dianlüe says: Zan exposed Yu in the market and prayed, saying, "If he ought to be Son of Heaven, let Heaven send rain to save him.
translations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe records that Zan displayed Yu in the marketplace and cried: "If Heaven wants this man as emperor, let rain spare him.

sentences.zh: 」時盛暑，竟日不雨，遂殺虞。

translations.literal: 」At the time it was sweltering summer; all day no rain, and he then killed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: 」It was the dog days; not a drop fell all day, and Zan killed him.

sentences.zh: 《英雄記》曰：虞之見殺，故常山相孫瑾、掾張逸、張瓚等忠義憤發，相與就虞，罵瓚極口，然後同死。〉

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: At Yu's execution, the former chancellor of Changshan Sun Jin and aides Zhang Yi and Zhang Zan, loyal and indignant, went to Yu together, cursed Zan to the utmost, then died together with him.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji adds that Sun Jin, Zhang Yi, and Zhang Zan went to the scaffold with Yu, reviled Zan to his face, and died beside him.〉

sentences.zh: 瓚上訓為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Zan memorialized Xun as governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had Xun named governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 瓚遂驕矜，記過忘善，多所賊害。

translations.literal: Zan thereupon grew arrogant and proud, recording faults and forgetting good, and did much killing and harm.
translations.idiomatic: He turned haughty, nursed grudges, forgot kindness, and shed much blood.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：瓚統內外，衣冠子弟有材秀者，必抑使困在窮苦之地。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Zan controlled inner and outer; for gentry youths who had talent and excellence, he always suppressed them so they were trapped in poor and bitter places.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji: Zan ran the region with an iron hand and broke any talented young gentleman by confining him to misery.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，答曰：「今取衣冠家子弟及善士富貴之，皆自以為職當得之，不謝人善也。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, he answered, saying, "Now if I take gentry sons and good men and enrich them, they all think office ought to come to them by right and do not thank others for their goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Spoil a wellborn man and he thinks rank his birthright and never remembers a favor.

sentences.zh: 」所寵遇驕恣者，類多庸兒，若故卜數師劉緯台、販繒李移子、賈人樂何當等三人，與之定兄弟之誓，自號為伯，謂三人者為仲叔季，富皆巨億，或取其女以配己子，常稱古者曲周、灌嬰之屬以譬也。〉

translations.literal: 」Those he favored and indulged in arrogance were mostly mediocre fellows, such as the former fortune-teller Liu Weitai, the silk peddler Li Yizi, and the merchant Le Hedang—three men—with whom he swore brotherhood, calling himself the eldest and the three the middle, second, and youngest; their wealth ran to hundreds of millions; he sometimes took their daughters to marry to his own sons, and often cited men of old like Qu Zhou and Guan Ying by way of comparison.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」His cronies were vulgarians like the diviner Liu Weitai, the cloth-seller Li Yizi, and the trader Le Hedang—sworn "brothers" he styled Bo while they were Zhong and Ji, each worth a fortune, whose daughters he married to his sons, likening the clique to ancient parvenus.〉

sentences.zh: 虞從事漁陽鮮于輔、齊周、騎都尉鮮于銀等，率州兵欲報瓚，以燕國閻柔素有恩信，共推柔為烏丸司馬。

translations.literal: Yu's clerk Xianyu Fu of Yuyang, Qi Zhou, chief of cavalry Xianyu Yin, and others led the provincial troops wishing to strike back at Zan; because Yan Rou of Yan always had grace and trust, they jointly pushed Rou as Wuhuan marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's aides Xianyu Fu, Qi Zhou, and Xianyu Yin raised the provincial host to settle scores with Zan and, trusting Yan Rou's name among the tribes, made him Wuhuan marshal.

sentences.zh: 柔招誘烏丸、鮮卑，得胡、漢數万人，與瓚所置漁陽太守鄒丹戰於潞北，大破之，斬丹。

translations.literal: Rou recruited and enticed Wuhuan and Xianbei, obtained Hu and Han several tens of thousands of men, and with Zan's appointed governor of Yuyang Zou Dan fought north of Lu, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Rou rallied Wuhuan and Xianbei, fielded tens of thousands of Hu and Han, met Zou Dan north of the Lu River, shattered him, and took his head.

sentences.zh: 袁紹又遣麴義及虞子和，將兵與輔合擊瓚。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao again sent Qu Yi and Yu's son He, leading troops to join Fu in striking Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent Qu Yi and Liu He to reinforce Xianyu Fu against Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚軍數敗，乃走還易京固守。

translations.literal: Zan's army was several times defeated, then fled back to Yi Jing and firmly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Zan lost repeatedly and fell back to his fortress at Yi Jing.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：先是有童謠曰：「燕南垂，趙北際，中央不合大如礪，惟有此中可避世。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Before there had been a children's rhyme saying, "South of Yan, north of Zhao, the center does not join, large as a whetstone; only within here may one escape the age."
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji: A rhyme ran, "South of Yan, north of Zhao, a gap wide as a grindstone—only there may you sit out the world."

sentences.zh: 」瓚以易當之，乃築京固守。

translations.literal: 」Zan took Yi as matching it, thereupon built Jing and firmly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zan read "Yi" into the verse and ringed himself in a fortress there.

sentences.zh: 瓚別將有為敵所圍，義不救也。

translations.literal: When Zan's other generals were surrounded by the enemy, he by righteousness did not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate commands were encircled, he refused relief on principle.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「救一人，使後將恃救不力戰；

translations.literal: His saying was: "If I rescue one man, later generals will rely on rescue and not fight with full effort;
translations.idiomatic: He argued, "Save one detachment and the next will count on a lifeline instead of fighting to the death;

sentences.zh: 今不救此，後將當念在自勉。

translations.literal: now if I do not rescue this, later generals will keep in mind that they must strive themselves.
translations.idiomatic: leave them to their fate and every commander will learn to stand alone."

sentences.zh: 」是以袁紹始北擊之時，瓚南界上別營自度守則不能自固，又知必不見救，是以或自殺其將帥，或為紹兵所破，遂令紹軍徑至其門。

translations.literal: 」Therefore when Yuan Shao first struck north, on Zan's southern border the separate camps, reckoning that if they defended they could not hold firm themselves, also knew they would certainly not see rescue, so some killed their own commanders, or were broken by Shao's troops, with the result that Shao's army went straight to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: 」So when Shao marched north, Zan's forward camps—knowing they could neither hold nor hope for help—mutinied or fell, and Shao's host rolled to his very gates.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為童謠之言，無不皆驗；

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that in the words of children's rhymes nothing fails of fulfillment;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that such ditties usually come true;

sentences.zh: 至如此記，似若無徵。

translations.literal: as for this record, it seems as if there is no verification.
translations.idiomatic: yet this anecdote hardly proves the point.

sentences.zh: 謠言之作，蓋令瓚終始保易，無事遠略。

translations.literal: The making of the rhyme, in general, was to make Zan from beginning to end keep to Yi and have no business with distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The rhyme rather urged Zan to cling to Yi and avoid grand designs.

sentences.zh: 而瓚因破黃巾之威，意志張遠，遂置三州刺史，圖滅袁氏，所以致敗也。〉

translations.literal: But Zan, because of the prestige of breaking the Yellow Turbans, his will and intent stretched far, thereupon set three provincial governors and plotted to destroy the Yuan clan, and therefore met defeat.〉
translations.idiomatic: Flush with his victory over the Yellow Turbans, he named three provincial chiefs and aimed to crush the Yuans—hence his ruin.〉

sentences.zh: 為圍塹十重，於塹裡築京，皆高五六丈，為樓其上；

translations.literal: He made tenfold encircling ditches; inside the ditches built Jing, all five or six fathoms high, and towers atop them;
translations.idiomatic: He dug ten rings of moats and raised ramparts five or six fathoms high inside them, crowned with watchtowers;

sentences.zh: 中塹為京，特高十丈，自居焉，積穀三百萬斛。

translations.literal: the central ditch's Jing was especially ten fathoms high; he himself dwelt there and stored grain to the amount of three million hu.
translations.idiomatic: the inner citadel rose ten fathoms; he lived at its core with three million hu of grain in store.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：瓚諸將家家各作高樓，樓以千計。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Each of Zan's generals' households separately built high towers, towers numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji: Every officer's household threw up a tower until thousands loomed over the camp.

sentences.zh: 瓚作鐵門，居樓上，屏去左右，婢妾侍側，汲上文書。〉

translations.literal: Zan made an iron gate, dwelt above on the tower, dismissed those at his left and right, with concubines and bondmaids attending at his side, drawing up documents by rope from below.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zan barred himself behind an iron gate on the parapet, dismissed attendants, kept only women at hand, and hauled orders up by cord.〉

sentences.zh: 瓚曰：「昔謂天下事可指麾而定，今日視之，非我所決，不如休兵，力田畜谷。

translations.literal: Zan said: "Formerly I said affairs of the empire could be settled with a wave of the hand; now looking at it, it is not for me to decide; better to rest the troops, labor the fields, and store grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zan said, "I once thought the realm could be ordered with a gesture; now I see it slips my grasp—better to disband for farming and fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 兵法，百樓不攻。

translations.literal: In military doctrine, a hundred towers cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War says a hundred towers need never fear assault.

sentences.zh: 今吾樓櫓千重，食盡此谷，足知天下之事矣。

translations.literal: Now my towers and bridges are a thousandfold; when this grain is eaten up, I shall know enough of the empire's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Here I have a thousand tiers of timber and grain enough to outwait any siege—then we shall see who rules the north."

sentences.zh: 」欲以此弊紹。

translations.literal: 」He wished thereby to exhaust Shao.
translations.idiomatic: 」He meant to wear Shao down.

sentences.zh: 紹遣將攻之，連年不能拔。

translations.literal: Shao sent generals to attack him; for successive years they could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's generals hammered at the place for years without breaching it.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：袁紹與瓚書曰：〉

translations.literal: 〈The Han Jin Chunqiu records Shao's letter to Zan, saying:〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin Annals preserves Shao's letter to Zan:〉

sentences.zh: 孤與足下，既有前盟舊要，申以討亂之誓，愛過夷、叔，分著丹青，謂為旅力同軌，足踵齊、晉，故解印釋紱，以北帶南，分割膏腴，以奉執事，此非孤赤情之明驗邪？

translations.literal: Between you and me, lonely one, there has already been a former covenant and old compact, reaffirmed by oaths to punish disorder; our love passed Bo Yi and Shu Qi, scored in cinnabar; I thought we would join strength on the same track, heel to heel with Qi and Jin; therefore I unsealed the ribbon and loosed the sash, linking north to south, dividing the fat lands to serve the steward—was this not the bright proof of my solitary red heart?
translations.idiomatic: You and I sealed old pacts and swore to purge rebels, love set down in vermilion ink like the martyrs Bo and Shu; I thought we would march as one with the hegemonies of Qi and Jin, so I laid down office, tied north to south, and carved out rich soil for your use—was that not candor?

sentences.zh: 豈寤足下棄烈士之高義，尋禍亡之險踪，輟而改慮，以好易怨，盜遣士馬，犯暴豫州。

translations.literal: How could I wake to find you casting aside the high righteousness of a martyr, tracing the perilous tracks of ruin and death, breaking off and changing your plan, exchanging goodwill for hatred, secretly dispatching soldiers and horses, invading and ravaging Yuzhou?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you spurned honor, chose the path of ruin, traded peace for feud, and sent troops to ravage Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 始聞甲卒在南，親臨戰陳，懼於飛矢迸流，狂刃橫集，以重足下之禍，徒增孤

translations.literal: When I first heard that armored soldiers had gone south and you personally entered the battle line, I feared flying arrows in swirling streams and wild blades crossing everywhere, which would deepen your lordship's disaster and only add to my
translations.idiomatic: When I learned your host had crossed south and you yourself had taken the field, I dreaded stray volleys and crossing steel—not only for your peril but because it would swell

translations.literal: (The manuscript carries the gloss zi, "son.")
translations.idiomatic: (A textual note inserts the character for "son.")

sentences.zh: 之咎釁也，故為薦書懇惻，冀可改悔。

translations.literal: burden of fault and shame; therefore I wrote letters in earnest sincerity, hoping you might repent and mend your ways.
translations.idiomatic: It would only swell my own burden of blame; I wrote earnestly in hope you would turn back.

sentences.zh: 而足下超然自逸，矜其威詐，謂天罔可吞，豪雄可滅，果令貴弟殞於鋒刃之端。

translations.literal: Yet you, lofty and self-ease, prided yourself on might and deceit, saying the net of Heaven could be swallowed and heroes extinguished, and in the end made your honored younger brother perish at the edge of blade and spear.
translations.idiomatic: You strutted instead, boasted you could swallow heaven and crush heroes, and let your cousin die on the spearpoints.

sentences.zh: 斯言猶在於耳，而足下曾不尋討禍源，克心罪己，苟欲逞其無疆之怒，不顧逆順之津，匿怨害民，聘於餘躬。

translations.literal: Those words are still in the ear, yet you never sought the source of the disaster, conquered your heart and blamed yourself, but wished only to give rein to boundless rage, heedless of the ford of obedience and rebellion, hiding resentment and harming the people, extending the quarrel to my humble person.
translations.idiomatic: The echo has not faded, yet you never searched out why the blow fell or owned your part; you only nursed boundless rage, ignored right and wrong, hurt the people, and dragged me into the feud.

sentences.zh: 遂躍馬控弦，處我疆土，毒遍生民，辜延白骨。

translations.literal: Thereupon you leaped on horse and grasped bow, stood on my territory, poison spread to the living people, guilt extended to white bones.
translations.idiomatic: You spurred onto my soil, poisoned the living, and piled the dead until the fields whitened with bone.

sentences.zh: 孤辭不獲已，以登界橋之役。

translations.literal: My humble words not having been obtained, I had to proceed to the affair of the battle at Jie Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Left no choice, I met you at Jie Bridge.

sentences.zh: 是時足下兵氣霆震，駿馬電發；

translations.literal: At that time your troops' qi was like thunder shaking; swift horses darted like lightning;
translations.idiomatic: Your host then shook like thunder, your chargers flashed like lightning;

sentences.zh: 僕師徒肇合，機械不嚴，強弱殊科，眾寡異論，假天之助，小戰大克，遂陵躡奔背，因壘館谷，此非天威棐諶，福豐有禮之符表乎？

translations.literal: my humble troops had just joined, machinery was not strict, strong and weak were of different grades, many and few were of different reckoning; borrowing Heaven's aid, in a small battle there was a great victory; thereupon I trod the fleeing backs, took grain from the enemy ramparts—is this not the tally of Heaven's majesty aiding the sincere and blessing the ritually right?
translations.idiomatic: my men were newly mustered, ill-drilled, odds uneven—yet heaven favored us: a skirmish became a rout, I rode down your retreat and fed my army from your camp—surely an omen that right stands with me?

sentences.zh: 足下志猶未厭，乃復糾合餘燼，率我蛑賊，以焚爇勃海。

translations.literal: Your foot's intent was still not satisfied, and again you gathered the remaining embers, led this caterpillar rabble, and burned Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Still unsated, you raked up embers, marched a locust swarm of raiders, and set Bohai ablaze.

sentences.zh: 孤又不獲寧，用及龍河之師。

translations.literal: My humble self again could not obtain peace, and therefore reached the army on the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Again I could not rest until I brought the host to the Long River line.

sentences.zh: 羸兵前誘，大軍未濟，而足下膽破眾散，不鼓而敗，兵眾擾亂，君臣並奔。

translations.literal: Weak troops lured you forward; the great army had not yet crossed when your courage broke and the host scattered, defeated without a drum, troops and masses in turmoil, ruler and ministers together fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: I baited you with a weak screen before the main body crossed; your nerve broke, your ranks melted without a stroke of the drum, lord and liegemen fled together.

sentences.zh: 此又足下之為，非孤之咎也。

translations.literal: This again was your doing, not my humble fault.
translations.idiomatic: That rout was your work, not mine.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，禍隙彌深，孤之師旅，不勝其忿，遂至積尸為京，頭顱滿野，愍彼無辜，未嘗不慨然失涕也。

translations.literal: From this time onward, the rift of disaster grew deeper; my humble troops could not overcome their wrath, with the result that piled corpses made a hill and skulls filled the wilds; pitying those without guilt, I have never failed to sigh and lose tears.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward hatred deepened; my soldiers, unable to curb their rage, heaped the dead into mounds—each time I think of the innocents I weep.

sentences.zh: 後比得足下書，辭意婉約，有改往脩來之言。

translations.literal: Later, comparing the letters I obtained from you, the wording was mild and contained words of mending the past and cultivating the future.
translations.idiomatic: Later your letters turned soft and spoke of healing the breach.

sentences.zh: 僕既欣於舊好克復，且愍兆民之不寧，每輒引師南駕，以順簡書。

translations.literal: Your servant both rejoiced that the old good could be restored, and pitied the hundred surnames' lack of peace; each time I therefore led the army southward, to comply with the bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: I welcomed the olive branch and pitied the people, so I drove south again as duty demanded.

sentences.zh: 弗盈一時，而北邊羽檄之文，未嘗不至。

translations.literal: Not full one season, yet documents of feathered urgency from the northern border never failed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Before a season passed, urgent dispatches from the northern marches arrived without fail.

sentences.zh: 孤是用痛心疾首，靡所錯情。

translations.literal: On that account I used pain in heart and ache in head, nowhere to place my feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Each left me heartsick, with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 夫處三軍之帥，當列將之任，宜令怒如嚴霜，喜如時雨，臧否好惡，坦然可觀。

translations.literal: One who stands as commander of three armies, holds the charge of arrayed generals, ought to make anger like severe frost and joy like seasonable rain, praise and blame, liking and loathing, plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: A commander of three armies should rage like hoarfrost and smile like spring rain, his likes and dislikes plain to all.

sentences.zh: 而足下二三其德，強弱易謀，急則曲躬，緩則放逸，行無定端，言無質要，為壯士者固若此乎！

translations.literal: Yet you twice and thrice your virtue, strong and weak change in plotting, urgent then crook the body, relaxed then let loose, action without fixed end, speech without substantive requirement—is it thus that one who is a stalwart man should solidly be!
translations.idiomatic: You shift allegiance with the wind, cringe when pressed and swagger when safe, act at random and promise nothing solid—is that how a warrior behaves?

sentences.zh: 既乃殘殺老弱，幽土怨，眾叛親離，孑然無黨。

translations.literal: Having then slaughtered the old and weak, Youzhou resented you, the host rebelled and kin departed, standing alone without a party.
translations.idiomatic: You butchered greybeards and children until Youzhou hated you, your men deserted and kinsmen fled, and you stood friendless.

sentences.zh: 又烏丸、濊貊，皆足下同州，僕與之殊俗，各奮迅激怒，爭為鋒銳；

translations.literal: Moreover the Wuhuan and Hui Mo are with you the same province; your servant with them is of different customs; each rouses swift fury and strives to be spear point and blade edge;
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan and Hui Mo share your province; I am a stranger to them—yet they race to my banner as vanguard steel;

sentences.zh: 又東西鮮卑，舉踵來附。

translations.literal: moreover east and west Xianbei lift heel and come to attach.
translations.idiomatic: east and west Xianbei flock in likewise.

sentences.zh: 此非孤德所能招，乃足下驅而致之也。

translations.literal: This is not what my humble virtue could summon; it is you who drove and brought them to it.
translations.idiomatic: That is not my virtue at work—you drove them into my arms.

sentences.zh: 夫當荒危之世，處干戈之險，內違同盟之誓，外失戎狄之心，兵興州壤，禍發蕭牆，將以定霸，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now in a generation of wilderness and peril, standing in the danger of spear and halberd, inwardly betraying the oath of allied hosts, outwardly losing the hearts of the Rong and Di, troops rise in the province's soil, disaster issues from the inner wall—intending thereby to fix hegemony, is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: In an age of arms, to break league oaths within and lose the tribes without, while mutiny stirs at home—how do you hope to win hegemony?

sentences.zh: 前以西山陸梁，出兵平討，會麴義餘殘，畏誅逃命，故遂住大軍，分兵撲盪，此兵孤之前行，乃界橋搴旗拔壘，先登制敵者也。

translations.literal: Formerly because the western hills were unruly, troops went out to pacify and punish; it happened that Qu Yi's remnants, fearing execution, fled for their lives, therefore the great army halted, divided troops to strike and scatter—this army of mine's vanguard, then at Jie Bridge plucked flags and pulled ramparts, was first to ascend and control the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the western hills rebelled I sent a column; Qu Yi's broken men fled the headsman, so I held the main force back while flying columns mopped up—the same van that stormed Jie Bridge and tore down your walls.

sentences.zh: 始聞足下鐫金紆紫，命以元帥，謂當因茲奮發，以報孟明之恥，是故戰夫引領，竦望旌旆，怪遂含光匿影，寂爾無聞，卒臻屠滅，相為惜之。

translations.literal: When I first heard that you carved gold and wound purple, were ordered commander-in-chief, I thought you would therefore rouse yourself to repay the shame of Meng Ming; therefore fighting men craned their necks, stood on tiptoe gazing at banners and pennants, wondered that you then hid radiance and concealed shadow, silent without report, in the end reaching slaughter and extinction—mutually I lament for you.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that you had taken gold seal and purple ribbon as supreme commander; I expected you to redeem yourself like Meng Ming—your soldiers watched the road for your banners—yet you hid, never stirred, and were cut to pieces. I pity you still.

sentences.zh: 夫有平天下之怒，希長世之功，權禦師徒，帶養戎馬，叛者無討，服者不收，威懷並喪，何以立名？

translations.literal: Now one who has anger to pacify the empire, hopes for merit lasting ages, controls and leads masters and troops, tends and nurtures war horses, does not punish rebels, does not gather those who submit—both awe and cherishing are lost; how shall he establish a name?
translations.idiomatic: A man who would rule the world must temper wrath with long strategy, feed his horses, punish traitors and shelter the loyal—lose both awe and kindness and what name remains?

sentences.zh: 今舊京克復，天罔雲補，罪人斯亡，忠幹翼化，華夏儼然，望於穆之作，將戢干戈，放散牛馬，足下獨何守區區之士，保內之廣，甘惡名以速朽，亡令德之久長？

translations.literal: Now the old capital has been recovered, Heaven's net is patched like clouds, the criminals are already gone, loyal stems wing transformation, Huaxia stands in awe, looking to the making of august Mu; we shall soon sheath spear and shield, turn oxen and horses loose to pasture—why do you alone cling to this scrap of soil and the breadth within your walls, willing to earn an evil name for a swift rotting, and not let lasting virtue endure long?
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is back in Han hands, the dynasty's net is mended, traitors swept away, loyal men rise to serve, and the heartland waits for a true restoration—we mean to stack arms and send the herds home—yet you hug a petty patch of ground, court infamy, and throw away a good name that might last.

sentences.zh: 壯而籌之，非良策也。

translations.literal: To be stalwart and scheme thus is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn scheming like that is poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 宜釋憾除嫌，敦我舊好。

translations.literal: You ought to drop old hurts and clear away suspicion, and thicken our former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Lay aside grudges, clear the air, and renew the bond we once had.

sentences.zh: 若斯言之玷，皇天是聞。

translations.literal: If there is a stain on these words, August Heaven hears.
translations.idiomatic: If I lie in what I say, let High Heaven hear it.

sentences.zh: 〈瓚不答，而增脩戎備。

translations.literal: 〈Zan did not answer but further repaired war preparations.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zan never replied; he only tightened his defenses.

sentences.zh: 謂關靖曰：「當今四方虎爭，無有能坐吾城下相守經年者明矣。

translations.literal: He said to Guan Jing: "Now the four quarters contend like tigers; clearly none can sit beneath our walls and hold each other for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: He told Guan Jing, "The realm is tearing itself apart; no one can camp under these walls and starve us out year after year.

sentences.zh: 袁本初其若我何！」〉

translations.literal: What can Yuan Benchu do to me!"〉
translations.idiomatic: What harm can Yuan Benchu really do me?"〉

sentences.zh: 建安四年，紹悉軍圍之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jian'an, Shao with his entire army besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 4 (199) Shao brought the full host to invest the fortress.

sentences.zh: 瓚遣子求救於黑山賊，复欲自將突騎直出，傍西南山，擁黑山之眾，陸梁冀州，橫斷紹後。

translations.literal: Zan sent his son to beg rescue of the Black Mountain bandits, and again wished personally to lead picked cavalry straight out along the southwestern hills, gather the Black Mountain masses, rampage through Jizhou, and cut Shao's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Zan dispatched his son to the Black Mountain chiefs and planned a breakout: picked cavalry down the southwest ranges to rally the hill bands, raid Ji province, and fall on Shao's rear.

sentences.zh: 長史關靖說瓚曰：「今將軍將士，皆已土崩瓦解，其所以能相守持者，顧戀其居處老小，以將軍為主耳。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Guan Jing urged Zan, saying: "Now the general's officers and men have all crumbled like earth and tiles; what lets them still hold together is only their attachment to home, old and young, and their looking to the general as their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jing warned him: "Your command is held together only by families clinging to this fort and to you as their chief.

sentences.zh: 將軍堅守曠日，袁紹要當自退；

translations.literal: If the general holds firm day after day, Yuan Shao in the end is bound himself to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast long enough and Shao must lift the siege;

sentences.zh: 自退之後，四方之眾必復可合也。

translations.literal: after he withdraws, the hosts of the four quarters can surely be gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: once he goes, you can rally support from every side again.

sentences.zh: 若將軍今舍之而去，軍無鎮重，易京之危，可立待也。

translations.literal: If the general now casts this aside and leaves, the army will have no anchor; the peril of Yi Jing can await you standing.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon the citadel now and you lose your base—Yi Jing will fall overnight.

sentences.zh: 將軍失本，孤在草野，何所成邪！

translations.literal: The general loses his root, stands orphaned in the wilds—what can be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Rootless on the open plain, what could you hope to accomplish?

sentences.zh: 」瓚遂止不出。

translations.literal: 」Zan thereupon stopped and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zan stayed put.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：關靖字士起，太原人。

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Guan Jing, courtesy name Shiqi, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji names Guan Jing, courtesy Shiqi, a Taiyuan man.

sentences.zh: 本酷吏也，諂而無大謀，特為瓚所信幸。〉

translations.literal: Originally a harsh clerk, fawning and without great plans, he was uniquely trusted and favored by Zan.〉
translations.idiomatic: A petty, flattering official without larger vision, he alone enjoyed Zan's trust.〉

sentences.zh: 救至，欲內外擊紹。

translations.literal: When rescue arrived, he wished to strike Shao from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When relief came, he meant to hit Shao inside and out.

sentences.zh: 遣人與子書，刻期兵至，舉火為應。

translations.literal: He sent a man to write his son, fixing a day when troops would arrive and raising fire as the signal.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to his son naming the day the column would come and bidding beacon fires as the sign.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：瓚遣行人文則齎書告子續曰：「袁氏之攻，似若神鬼，鼓角鳴於地中，梯衝舞吾樓上。

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe says: Zan sent traveling clerk Wen Ze bearing a letter to tell his son Xu: "The Yuan assault is like gods and ghosts; drums and horns sound from the earth, scaling ladders and rams dance atop our towers.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Dianlüe: Zan's courier Wen Ze carried a letter to Xu: "The Yuan siege feels supernatural—drums seem to rise from the ground, ladders and rams swarm our parapets.

sentences.zh: 日窮月蹴，無所聊賴。

translations.literal: Day by day we are pressed to extremity; there is nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: We are worn down day and night with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 汝當碎首於張燕，速致輕騎，到者當起烽火於北，吾當從內出。

translations.literal: You ought to dash your brains out before Zhang Yan, speedily bring light cavalry; when they arrive you must raise beacon fires on the north, and I shall sally from within.
translations.idiomatic: Grovel before Zhang Yan if you must, but bring light cavalry at once; when they arrive, light the northern beacons and I will burst out from within.

sentences.zh: 不然，吾亡之後，天下雖廣，汝欲求安足之地，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Otherwise, after I am gone, though the empire is vast, will you be able to find a piece of ground where your feet can rest in peace!"
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, when I am dead and the realm is wide, where will you find a haven?"

sentences.zh: 」《獻帝春秋》曰：瓚夢薊城崩，知必敗，乃遣間使與續書。

translations.literal: 」The Xiandi Chunqiu says: Zan dreamed the city of Ji collapsing, knew he must be defeated, then sent a secret messenger with a letter to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Xiandi Chunqiu adds that Zan dreamed Ji city falling, saw doom ahead, and smuggled a letter to Xu.

sentences.zh: 紹候者得之，使陳琳更其書曰：「蓋聞在昔衰周之世，僵戶流血，以為不然，豈意今日身當其衝！

translations.literal: Shao's watcher intercepted it and had Chen Lin rewrite the letter, saying: "I have heard that in the bygone age of declining Zhou, stiff corpses and flowing blood—I did not believe it; who would have thought today my own body should bear that shock!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao's scouts seized it; Chen Lin forged a reply: "They say the late Zhou left corpses in rivers of blood—I never believed it—until I felt the blow myself!"

sentences.zh: 」其餘語與《典略》所載同。〉

translations.literal: The remaining language is the same as what the Dianlüe records.〉
translations.idiomatic: The rest matches the Dianlüe text.〉

sentences.zh: 紹侯者得其書，如期舉火。

translations.literal: Shao's watcher obtained the letter and on the appointed day raised the fires.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's pickets lit the fires on schedule.

sentences.zh: 瓚以為救兵至，遂出欲戰。

translations.literal: Zan thought rescue troops had arrived, then went out wishing to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zan took the signal for relief and sallied to give battle.

sentences.zh: 紹設伏擊，大破之，復還守。

translations.literal: Shao set an ambush and struck him, greatly defeated him, and he again returned to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's ambush shattered the sortie and drove him back behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 紹為地道，突壞其樓，稍至中京。

translations.literal: Shao dug tunnels, burst and broke his towers, and gradually reached the central Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sappers undermined the towers until they reached the inner keep.

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：袁紹分部攻者掘地為道，穿穴其樓下，稍稍施木柱之，度足達半，便燒所施之柱，樓輒傾倒。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong Ji says: Yuan Shao's partial divisions of attackers dug the ground into tunnels, pierced beneath their towers, gradually set wooden props, estimated when they had reached halfway, then burned the props they had set, and the towers then collapsed.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yingxiong Ji: Shao's teams tunneled under the ramparts, shored the galleries with timber, burned the props at mid-course, and brought the towers down.〉

sentences.zh: 瓚自知必敗，盡殺其妻子，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Zan knew himself bound to be defeated, killed his wife and children to the last, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the end, Zan slaughtered his family and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：關靖曰：「吾聞君子陷人於危，必同其難，豈可獨生乎！

translations.literal: 〈The Han Jin Chunqiu says: Guan Jing said: "I have heard that when a gentleman has trapped another in peril, he must share the hardship—how can he live alone!"
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin Annals: Guan Jing said, "A gentleman does not leave a man in danger and walk away—how could I survive alone?"

sentences.zh: 」乃策馬赴紹軍而死。

translations.literal: 」Then he spurred his horse into Shao's army and died.
translations.idiomatic: 」He spurred into Shao's lines and died there.

sentences.zh: 紹悉送其首於許。〉

translations.literal: Shao sent all their heads to Xu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Shao shipped the heads to the capital at Xu.〉

sentences.zh: 鮮于輔將其眾奉王命。

translations.literal: Xianyu Fu led his host in obedience to the king's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu brought his troops over to the Han side.

sentences.zh: 以輔為建忠將軍，督幽州六郡。

translations.literal: Fu was appointed general who establishes loyalty and charged to superintend six commanderies of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him general who establishes loyalty and set him over six Youzhou commanderies.

sentences.zh: 太祖與袁紹相拒於官渡，閻柔遣使詣太祖受事，遷護烏丸校尉。
