translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor opposed Yuan Shao at Guandu, Yan Rou sent an envoy to the Grand Progenitor to receive appointment and was promoted colonel protecting the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu, Yan Rou sent envoys to Cao Cao, took orders, and was raised to colonel protecting the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 而輔身詣太祖，拜左度遼將軍，封亭侯，遣還鎮撫本州。

translations.literal: Fu himself went to the Grand Progenitor, was appointed general who crosses Liao on the left, enfeoffed village marquis, and was sent back to pacify and console his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu went in person, became general who crosses Liao on the left, received a village marquisate, and returned to pacify Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：輔從太祖於官渡。

translations.literal: 〈The Weilüe says: Fu followed the Grand Progenitor at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe: Fu campaigned with Cao Cao at Guandu.

sentences.zh: 袁紹破走，太祖喜，顧謂輔曰：「如前歲本初送公孫瓚頭來，孤自視忽然耳，而今克之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao was broken and fled, the Grand Progenitor rejoiced, turned and said to Fu: "The year before last when Benchu sent Gongsun Zan's head, I looked at myself as if in a trance; now we have overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao broke and ran, Cao Cao turned to Fu and said, "When Benchu sent me Zan's head I could scarcely believe my eyes; now we have beaten the man himself.

sentences.zh: 此既天意，亦二三子之力。」〉

translations.literal: This is both Heaven's intent and the force of you several gentlemen."〉
translations.idiomatic: This is heaven's will—and yours as well."〉

sentences.zh: 太祖破南皮，柔將部曲及鮮卑獻名馬以奉軍，從征三郡烏丸，以功封關內侯。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took Nanpi, Rou led his following troops and Xianbei to present famous horses for the army's use, followed the expedition against the Wuhuan of three commanderies, and on merit was enfeoffed marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanpi fell, Rou brought retainers and Xianbei to offer famous horses, joined the three-Wuhuan campaign, and earned a marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖甚愛閻柔，每謂之曰：「我視卿如子，亦欲卿視我如父也。

translations.literal: 〈The Weilüe says: The Grand Progenitor greatly loved Yan Rou and often said to him: "I look on you as a son and also wish you to look on me as a father.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe: Cao Cao doted on Yan Rou and often said, "I treat you as a son; I want you to treat me as a father."

sentences.zh: 」柔由此自託於五官將，如兄弟。〉

translations.literal: 」Rou from this entrusted himself to the heir apparent of the five offices, like brothers.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」Rou thereafter attached himself to the heir apparent as to an elder brother.〉

sentences.zh: 輔亦率其眾從。

translations.literal: Fu likewise led his host to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Fu marched his men in the same service.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，拜輔虎牙將軍，柔度遼將軍，皆進封縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Fu was appointed general of tiger fangs and Rou general who crosses Liao; both were advanced to county marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen raised Fu to general of tiger fangs and Rou to general who crosses Liao, each with a county marquisate.

sentences.zh: 位特進。

translations.literal: Their rank reached extraordinary advance.
translations.idiomatic: Both rose to extraordinary advance in rank.

sentences.zh: 陶謙字恭祖，丹楊人。

translations.literal: Tao Qian, courtesy name Gongzu, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian, whose courtesy name was Gongzu, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：謙父，故餘姚長。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: Qian's father was formerly magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu: his father had been magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 謙少孤，始以不羈聞於縣中。

translations.literal: Qian in youth was orphaned and first became known in the county for an unbridled spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was already known county-wide for wild high spirits.

sentences.zh: 年十四，猶綴帛爲幡，乘竹馬而戲，邑中兒僮皆隨之。

translations.literal: At fourteen he still stitched silk into banners, rode a bamboo horse in play, and all the boys of the town followed him.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he sewed silk pennons, rode a bamboo hobbyhorse, and every lad in town trailed after him.

sentences.zh: 故蒼梧太守同縣甘公出遇之塗，見其容貌，異而呼之，住車與語，甚恱，因許妻以女。

translations.literal: The former governor of Cangwu, Duke Gan of the same county, met him on the road, marveled at his looks, called him over, stopped his carriage, and spoke with him; greatly pleased, he promised him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Gong of Cangwu, a townsman, met him in the street, was struck by his face, halted his carriage, talked until delighted, and betrothed a daughter.

sentences.zh: 甘公夫人聞之，怒曰：「妾聞陶家兒敖戲無度，如何以女許之？

translations.literal: Madam Gan heard it and angrily said: "I have heard the Tao boy plays without restraint—how can you give him our daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gan fumed, "That Tao boy is all mischief—why marry our girl to him?"

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「彼有奇表，長必大成。

translations.literal: The duke said: "He has an extraordinary bearing; grown, he is sure to achieve greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Gan answered, "His looks are not common; grown, he will be someone."

sentences.zh: 」遂妻之。〉

translations.literal: 」Then he gave her to him in marriage.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」And he did give her to him.〉

sentences.zh: 少好學，爲諸生，仕州邵，舉茂才，除盧令，

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, became a student, served in the province and commandery, was recommended flourishing talent, and was appointed magistrate of Lu,
translations.idiomatic: He studied as a young man, entered provincial service, earned a flourishing-talent recommendation, and became magistrate of Lu,

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：謙性剛直，有大節，少察孝廉，拜尚書郎，除舒令。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: Qian's nature was sternly upright with great integrity; in youth he was examined filial and incorrupt, appointed gentleman of the masters of writing, and removed as magistrate of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu adds that he was stern, high-principled, filial-and-incorrupt, a masters-of-writing gentleman, then magistrate of Shu.

sentences.zh: 郡守張磐，同郡先輩，與謙父友意殊親之，而謙恥爲之屈。

translations.literal: The commandery governor Zhang Pan, an elder townsman, was on friendly terms with Qian's father in intention especially close, yet Qian was ashamed to bend before him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Pan, an elder from the same commandery and his father's intimate friend, favored him—yet Qian hated to bow.

sentences.zh: 與衆還城，因以公事進見，坐罷，磐常私還入與謙飲宴，或拒不爲留。

translations.literal: Returning to the city with the host, he therefore on public business went in to audience; when the session ended, Pan often privately returned to drink and feast with Qian, but sometimes Qian refused and would not stay.
translations.idiomatic: After a public session Pan would invite him to drink; Qian often snubbed the invitation.

sentences.zh: 常以舞屬謙，謙不爲起，固彊之；

translations.literal: Pan often made the dance belong to Qian; Qian would not rise for it, and Pan forced him;
translations.idiomatic: Pan tried to make him lead the dance; Qian would not stand though pressed;

sentences.zh: 及舞，又不轉。

translations.literal: when it came to the dance, again he would not turn.
translations.idiomatic: when he did move, he refused to turn.

sentences.zh: 磐曰：「不當轉邪？

translations.literal: Pan said: "Ought one not to turn?"
translations.idiomatic: Pan asked, "Are you not supposed to wheel?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不可轉，轉則勝人。

translations.literal: He said: "One must not turn; to turn is to outdo others."
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied, "I must not turn—turning means showing up the host."

sentences.zh: 」由是不樂，卒以搆隙。

translations.literal: 」From this Pan was unhappy, and in the end they developed a rift.
translations.idiomatic: 」Pan took offense and a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 謙在官清白，無以糾舉，祠靈星，有贏錢五百，欲以臧之。

translations.literal: Qian in office was pure and white, with nothing to impeach; he sacrificed to the Ling star and had a surplus of five hundred cash, wishing to hide it away.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he was spotless; after a Ling-star sacrifice five hundred cash remained, which he meant to pocket.

sentences.zh: 謙委官而去。〉

translations.literal: Qian cast aside office and left.〉
translations.idiomatic: Instead he resigned his post.〉

sentences.zh: 遷幽州剌史，徵拜議郎，參車騎將軍張溫軍事，西討韓遂。

translations.literal: He was transferred governor of Youzhou, summoned and appointed gentleman consultant, joined the military affairs of General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Wen, and marched west to punish Han Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Youzhou, then consultant, joined Zhang Wen's staff, and campaigned west against Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：會西羌寇邊，皇甫嵩爲征西將軍，表請武將。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: It happened that the western Qiang raided the border; Huangfu Song became general who campaigns west and memorialized requesting martial officers.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu: when western Qiang raided the frontier, Huangfu Song, as western campaign general, asked for fighting men.

sentences.zh: 召拜謙楊武都尉，與嵩征羌，大破之。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Qian valorous martial commandant of Yang, and with Song campaigned against the Qiang and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was named valorous martial commandant of Yang and routed the Qiang with Huangfu Song.

sentences.zh: 後邊章、韓遂爲亂，司空張溫銜命征討；

translations.literal: Later Bian Zhang and Han Sui made rebellion; Minister of Works Zhang Wen bore mandate to campaign and punish;
translations.idiomatic: Later Bian Zhang and Han Sui rose; Minister of Works Zhang Wen took the field;

sentences.zh: 又請謙爲參軍事，接遇甚厚，而謙輕其行事，心懷不服。

translations.literal: again he requested Qian as aide in military affairs, received him with very great favor, but Qian despised his conduct of affairs and harbored discontent in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: he made Qian an army aide and treated him generously, yet Qian scorned his leadership and nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 及軍罷還，百寮高會，溫屬謙行酒，謙衆辱溫。

translations.literal: When the army ceased and returned, the hundred officials held a high gathering; Wen assigned Qian to pass the wine, and Qian in the crowd humiliated Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the victory feast Zhang Wen told Qian to pour wine; Qian publicly insulted him.

sentences.zh: 溫怒，徙謙於邊。

translations.literal: Wen was angry and banished Qian to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wen banished him to the border.

sentences.zh: 或說溫曰：「陶恭祖本以材略見重於公，一朝以醉飲過失，不蒙容貸，遠棄不毛，厚德不終，四方人士安所歸望！

translations.literal: Someone urged Wen, saying: "Tao Gongzu was originally valued by you, lord, for talent and strategy; in one morning, because of a drunken slip, he did not receive tolerant pardon but was cast far into barren land—your thick virtue does not reach its end; where shall men of the four quarters turn their hopes!
translations.idiomatic: Counselors said, "You prized Tao Gongzu for ability; one drunk slight, and you ship him to the wastes—how will the world trust your magnanimity?"

sentences.zh: 不如釋憾除恨，克復初分，於以遠聞德美。

translations.literal: Better to drop old hurts and clear away hatred, restore the original bond, and thereby let your virtuous beauty be heard from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Better forgive him, heal the rift, and let your name for mercy spread."

sentences.zh: 」溫然其言，乃追還謙。

translations.literal: 」Wen approved his words and then recalled Qian.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wen agreed and recalled Qian.

sentences.zh: 謙至，或又謂謙曰：「足下輕辱三公，罪自己作，今蒙釋宥，德莫厚矣；

translations.literal: When Qian arrived, someone again said to Qian: "You lightly insulted the three dukes; the crime was your own doing; now you have received release and forgiveness—no grace could be thicker;
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Qian on return, "You humiliated a minister of state; the fault was yours; now you are pardoned—no kindness could run deeper;

sentences.zh: 宜降志卑辭以謝之。

translations.literal: you ought to lower your will and humble your words to apologize to him.
translations.idiomatic: humble yourself and apologize."

sentences.zh: 」謙曰：「諾。

translations.literal: 」Qian said, "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: 」Qian said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 」又謂溫曰：「陶恭祖今深自罪責，思在變革。

translations.literal: 」He also said to Wen: "Tao Gongzu now deeply blames himself and thinks of reform.
translations.idiomatic: The same man told Wen, "Tao Gongzu repents deeply and means to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 謝天子禮畢，必詣公門。

translations.literal: When he has finished apologizing to the Son of Heaven in ritual, he is sure to come to your gate.
translations.idiomatic: After he has made ritual apology to the throne he will call on you.

sentences.zh: 公宜見之，以慰其意。

translations.literal: You, lord, ought to receive him to console his mind.
translations.idiomatic: You should receive him to set his mind at ease."

sentences.zh: 」時溫於宮門見謙，謙仰曰：「謙自謝朝廷，豈爲公邪？

translations.literal: 」At the time Wen met Qian at the palace gate; Qian looked up and said: "Qian apologizes to the court—was it for you, lord?"
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate Qian looked up and said, "I bow to the court—not to you."

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「恭祖癡病尚未除邪？

translations.literal: 」Wen said: "Has Gongzu's foolish sickness not yet been removed?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen snapped, "Is Gongzu still mad?"

sentences.zh: 」遂爲之置酒，待之如初。〉

translations.literal: 」Thereupon for him he set wine and treated him as at first.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」Yet Wen poured wine and treated him as before.〉

sentences.zh: 會徐州黃巾起，以謙爲徐州剌史，擊黃巾，破走之。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans of Xuzhou rose, Qian was made governor of Xuzhou, attacked the Yellow Turbans, and broke and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuzhou's Yellow Turbans rose, he was named governor, crushed them, and drove them out.

sentences.zh: 董卓之亂，州郡起兵，天子都長安，四方斷絕，謙遣使間行致貢獻，遷安東將軍、徐州牧，封溧陽侯。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, provinces and commanderies raised troops; the Son of Heaven had his capital at Chang'an; the four quarters were cut off; Qian sent envoys by secret routes to present tribute; he was promoted general who pacifies the east, shepherd of Xuzhou, and enfeoffed marquis of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhuo's reign of terror, while the emperor languished in Chang'an and roads were cut, Qian smuggled tribute west, won the title general who pacifies the east, shepherd of Xuzhou, and marquis of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，徐州百姓殷盛，穀米封贍，流民多歸之。

translations.literal: At this time the hundred surnames of Xuzhou were prosperous and abundant, grain and rice piled high in surplus, and drifting people for the most part returned to it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou then overflowed with grain and drew refugees from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 而謙背道任情：廣陵太守琅邪趙昱，徐方名士也，以忠直見疏；

translations.literal: But Qian turned his back on the Way and followed his whim: Zhao Yu of Langya, governor of Guangling, a famous gentleman of the Xu region, because of loyalty and uprightness was kept at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qian ruled by caprice: Zhao Yu of Guangling, a leading scholar of the east, was shunned for his honesty;

sentences.zh: 〈謝承《漢書》曰：昱年十三，母嘗病，經涉三月。

translations.literal: 〈Xie Cheng's Hanshu says: When Yu was thirteen, his mother once was ill, passing through three months.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xie Cheng's Hanshu: at thirteen Yu nursed his sick mother three months,

sentences.zh: 昱慘戚消瘠，至目不交睫，握粟出卜，祈禱泣血，鄉黨稱其孝。

translations.literal: Yu was haggard and emaciated, to the point that his eyes did not close in sleep; he grasped millet and went out to divine, prayed and wept blood; the township praised his filiality.
translations.idiomatic: withered with grief, never sleeping, divined with millet, wept blood in prayer, and won praise for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 就處士東莞綦毌君受《公羊傳》，兼該羣業。

translations.literal: He went to the reclusive gentleman Jun Qi of Dongguan to receive the Gongyang commentary, comprehending the mass of learning.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Gongyang with recluse Jun Qi of Dongguan and mastered many texts.

sentences.zh: 至歷年潛志，不闚園圃，親疏希見其面。

translations.literal: For successive years he submerged his will, did not peep at gardens, and intimate and distant seldom saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: For years he shut himself in study, shunned gardens, and rarely showed his face.

sentences.zh: 時入定省父母，須臾即還。

translations.literal: At times he entered to inquire after his parents and in a moment returned.
translations.idiomatic: Even visits to his parents were brief.

sentences.zh: 高絜廉正，抱禮而立，清英儼恪，莫干其志；

translations.literal: Lofty, pure, honest, and upright, embracing ritual he stood; clear brilliance stern and reverent—none could shake his purpose;
translations.idiomatic: He was austere, incorruptible, and grave—none could sway him;

sentences.zh: 旌善以興化，彈邪以矯俗。

translations.literal: he raised the good to enact transformation and struck the wicked to correct custom.
translations.idiomatic: he honored virtue to improve custom and struck down vice.

sentences.zh: 州郡請召，常稱病不應。

translations.literal: When provinces and commanderies summoned him, he always claimed illness and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every summons with feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 國相檀謨、陳遵比召，不起；

translations.literal: The chancellor Tan Mo and Chen Zun together summoned him and he did not rise;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Tan Mo and Chen Zun called together—he would not come;

sentences.zh: 或興盛怒，終不迴意。

translations.literal: sometimes they roused great anger, yet in the end he did not change his mind.
translations.idiomatic: even their fury could not move him.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，除莒長，宣揚五教，政爲國表。

translations.literal: He was recommended filial and incorrupt, appointed magistrate of Ju, spread abroad the five teachings, and his government became a model for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he governed Ju, taught the five moral relations, and set the standard for the realm.

sentences.zh: 會黃巾作亂，陸梁五郡，郡縣發兵，以爲先辦。

translations.literal: When it happened that the Yellow Turbans made rebellion, rampaging across five commanderies, commanderies and counties raised troops, taking that as the first task.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turbans rose and overran five commanderies, every county mustered arms as top priority.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史巴祗表功第一，當受遷賞，昱深以爲恥，委官還家。

translations.literal: The inspector of Xuzhou Ba Zhi memorialized his merit as first and that he should receive promotion and reward; Yu deeply took it as shame and cast aside office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Ba Zhi ranked his service first for promotion; Yu took that as an insult and resigned.

sentences.zh: 徐州牧陶謙初辟別駕從事，辭疾遜遁。

translations.literal: Shepherd of Xuzhou Tao Qian first summoned him as aide-de-camp; he pleaded illness and yielded the post.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian then governor summoned him as chief clerk; he feigned illness and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 謙重令楊州從事會稽吳範宣旨，昱守意不移；

translations.literal: Qian again ordered Yangzhou clerk Wu Fan of Kuaiji to proclaim the edict; Yu held his resolve unmoved;
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent Wu Fan of Kuaiji from the Yangzhou office to press the appointment; Yu would not budge;

sentences.zh: 欲威以刑罰，然後乃起。

translations.literal: he wished to awe him with punishments, and only then did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: Qian threatened the law until Yu finally accepted.

sentences.zh: 舉茂才，遷廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He was recommended flourishing talent and transferred to governor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a flourishing-talent nomination and became governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 賊笮融從臨淮見討，迸入郡界，昱將兵拒戰，敗績，見害。〉

translations.literal: The bandit Ze Rong, pursued from Linhuai, burst into the commandery borders; Yu led troops to resist in battle, was defeated, and was killed.〉
translations.idiomatic: Ze Rong, driven from Linhuai, broke into the district; Yu fought him, lost, and died.〉

sentences.zh: 曹宏等，讒慝小人也，謙親任之。

translations.literal: Cao Hong and others were petty men of slander and evil; Qian personally trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Cao Hong were venal flatterers, yet Qian kept them close.

sentences.zh: 刑政失和，良善多被其害，由是漸亂。

translations.literal: Punishments and government lost harmony; the good for the most part suffered harm at their hands; from this it gradually fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Justice skewed and honest men suffered; the province slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 下邳闕宣自稱天子，謙初與合從寇鈔，後遂殺宣，并其衆。

translations.literal: Que Xuan of Xiapi styled himself Son of Heaven; Qian at first joined him in horizontal alliance to plunder, afterward then killed Xuan and annexed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Que Xuan at Xiapi declared himself emperor; Qian first allied with him for raids, then killed him and swallowed his troops.

sentences.zh: 初平四年，太祖征謙，攻拔十餘城，至彭城大戰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuping, the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Qian, attacked and took more than ten cities, and reached Pengcheng for a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping 4 (193) Cao Cao struck Qian, stormed a dozen towns, and fought a major battle at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 謙兵敗走，死者萬數，泗水爲之不流。

translations.literal: Qian's troops were defeated and fled; the dead numbered in the myriads, and the Si River for it did not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's army broke; corpses choked the Si until the current stalled.

sentences.zh: 謙退守剡。

translations.literal: Qian withdrew to defend Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fell back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 太祖以糧少引軍還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because grain was scant led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Short of supplies, Cao Cao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：曹公父於泰山被殺，歸咎於謙。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: Lord Cao's father was killed on Mount Tai, and the blame was laid on Qian.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu: Cao Song was murdered in Taishan, and Cao Cao blamed Qian.

sentences.zh: 欲伐謙而畏其彊，乃表令州郡一時罷兵。

translations.literal: He wished to attack Qian but feared his strength, therefore memorialized ordering provinces and commanderies for the moment to disband troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting war yet fearing Qian's power, he petitioned for a general stand-down of provincial armies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今海內擾攘，州郡起兵，征夫勞瘁，寇難未弭，或將吏不良，因緣討捕，侵侮黎民，離害者衆；

translations.literal: The edict said: "Now within the seas there is turmoil; provinces and commanderies have raised troops; the levied men are weary and haggard; bandit troubles are not yet quieted; perhaps generals and clerks are not good, and relying on pursuit and capture they encroach on and insult the black-haired people—those separated and harmed are many;
translations.idiomatic: The edict ran: "The realm is in turmoil, troops are everywhere, soldiers are spent, bandits remain—often because officers prey on civilians;

sentences.zh: 風聲流聞，震蕩城邑，丘牆懼於橫暴，貞良化爲羣惡，此何異乎抱薪救焚，扇火止沸哉！

translations.literal: the wind of rumor spreads and shakes cities and towns; humble walls fear violence; the chaste and good turn into packs of evil—how is this different from hugging firewood to save a blaze or fanning a fire to stop boiling!"
translations.idiomatic: rumor panics towns, the meek turn rogue—like piling fuel on a fire or fanning a boiling pot!"

sentences.zh: 今四民流移，託身佗方，攜白首於山野，棄稚子於溝壑，顧故鄉而哀歎，向阡陌而流涕，饑厄困苦，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: Now the four peoples drift and move, entrusting themselves to other regions, carrying white heads in mountain wilds, casting young children into gullies and ravines, looking toward the old village and sighing in grief, facing field paths and shedding tears; hunger, peril, hardship, and bitterness have already reached the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Common folk flee to strange lands, leave elders in the hills and infants in ditches, weep for home and starve in exile—the suffering is extreme."

sentences.zh: 雖悔往者之迷謬，思奉教於今日，然兵連衆結，鋒鏑布野，恐一朝解散，夕見繫虜，是以阻兵屯據，欲止而不敢散也。

translations.literal: Although they regret former errors and wish today to obey instruction, yet troops are linked and hosts bound, spear points and arrowheads spread over the wilds; I fear that if in one morning they disband, at evening they will be seen bound captive; therefore they block troops and hold fast, wishing to stop yet not daring to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: They would lay down arms, yet fear that the day they disband they will be chains by night—so they cling to their camps."

sentences.zh: 詔書到，其各罷遣甲士，還親農桑，惟留常員吏以供官署，慰示遠近，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, let each disband and send away armored soldiers, return to dear ones and farming and sericulture; only leave the regular complement of clerks to supply the offices; console and show far and near, and cause all to hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: Let every command send farmers home, keep only routine clerks, and publish the mercy far and wide."

sentences.zh: 」謙被詔，乃上書曰：「臣聞懷遠柔服，非德不集；

translations.literal: 」When Qian received the edict, he then submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that cherishing the distant and softening submission does not gather without virtue;
translations.idiomatic: 」Qian answered: "Winning distant peoples takes virtue;

sentences.zh: 克難平亂，非兵不濟。

translations.literal: overcoming difficulty and pacifying disorder is not helped without troops.
translations.idiomatic: crushing rebels takes soldiers."

sentences.zh: 是以涿鹿、版泉、三苗之野有五帝之師，有扈、鬼方、商、奄四國有王者之伐，自古在昔，未有不揚威以弭亂，震武以止暴者也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the wilds of Zhuolu, Banquan, and the three Miao there were the armies of the five emperors; against Youhu, Guifang, Shang, and Yan—the four states—there were the punishments of the kingly man; from of old in the past there has never been one who did not display might to quiet disorder and shake martial power to stop violence.
translations.idiomatic: The five sage-kings marched to Zhuolu and Banquan; kings struck Youhu, Guifang, Shang, and Yan—never yet did a throne end violence without showing the sword."

sentences.zh: 臣前初以黃巾亂治，受策長驅，匪遑啟處。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier at first because the Yellow Turbans disturbed order, received the tally and drove long, without leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turbans first rose I took the commission and rode the long campaign without rest."

sentences.zh: 雖憲章勑戒，奉宣威靈，敬行天誅，每伐輒克，然妖寇類衆，殊不畏死，父兄殲殪，子弟羣起，治屯連兵，至今爲患。

translations.literal: Although statutes and ordinances warned and admonished, reverently carrying out awesome power and respectfully executing Heaven's punishments, each attack then succeeded, yet the demon bandits are many in kind and utterly do not fear death; fathers and elder brothers are exterminated, sons and younger brothers rise in groups, set camps and link troops, down to the present making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: We obeyed the law and struck heaven's foes, and each battle won—yet the rebels are countless, fearless of death; clans refill their ranks and camp against us still."

sentences.zh: 若承命解甲，弱國自虛，釋武備以資亂，損官威以益寇，今日兵罷，明日難必至，上忝朝廷寵授之本，下令羣凶日月滋蔓，非所以彊幹弱枝遏惡止亂之務也。

translations.literal: If I obey the command to lay aside armor, the weak state will empty itself; I would release military preparation to supply disorder, injure official awe to increase bandits; today the troops cease, tomorrow disaster is sure to arrive; above I would disgrace the root of court favor in appointing me, below I would order the many villains daily to grow and spread—this is not the task of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, checking evil and stopping disorder.
translations.idiomatic: To stack arms now would strip a weak province, arm the enemy, and shame the court that trusted me—while villains grow daily; that is not how to strengthen the center and choke rebellion."

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚蔽，忠恕不昭，抱恩念報，所不忍行。

translations.literal: Your subject though foolish and dim, loyalty and forgiveness not clear, embracing grace and thinking of repayment—what I cannot bear to do.
translations.idiomatic: I am a dull man, yet I cannot betray the favor I owe."

sentences.zh: 輒勒部曲，申令警備。

translations.literal: I therefore urge my following troops and repeat orders for alert defense.
translations.idiomatic: I have drilled my command and doubled the watch."

sentences.zh: 出芟彊寇，惟力是視，入宣德澤，躬奉職事，冀效微勞，以贖罪負。

translations.literal: Going out I mow down strong bandits, looking only to strength; entering I spread virtuous moisture and personally perform duties, hoping to render slight labor to redeem my burden of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I strike rebels abroad and rule kindly at home, hoping to atone in small measure."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「華夏沸擾，于今未弭，包茅不入，職貢多闕，寤寐憂歎，無日敢寧。

translations.literal: 」He also said: "Huaxia boils and is disturbed; to the present it is not quieted; the bundle of sedge does not enter, tribute and duties are much lacking; waking and sleeping I sigh in worry; no day do I dare be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The heartland still seethes; the king lacks even the ritual bundle of sedge; I lie awake grieving."

sentences.zh: 誠思貢獻必至，薦羞獲通，然後銷鋒解甲，臣之願也。

translations.literal: Truly I think that when contributions surely arrive and recommended viands obtain passage, then melting spear points and loosing armor—that is your subject's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Only when my grain reaches the throne and roads are open will I sheathe the sword—that is my prayer."

sentences.zh: 臣前調穀百萬斛，已在水次，輒勑兵衞送。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier requisitioned grain to the amount of one million hu; it is already at the water's edge; I have ordered troops to escort it.
translations.idiomatic: I have a million hu of grain barged and ready; escorts stand by to send it."

sentences.zh: 」曹公得謙上事，知不罷兵。

translations.literal: 」When Lord Cao obtained Qian's memorial, he knew he would not disband troops.
translations.idiomatic: 」Cao Cao read the reply and saw Qian would not demobilize.

sentences.zh: 乃進攻彭城，多殺人民。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Pengcheng and killed many of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again on Pengcheng and massacred civilians.

sentences.zh: 謙引兵擊之，青州刺史田楷亦以兵救謙。

translations.literal: Qian led troops to strike him; the governor of Qingzhou Tian Kai also brought troops to rescue Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Qian counterattacked; Tian Kai of Qingzhou marched to his aid.

sentences.zh: 公引兵還。

translations.literal: The lord led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pulled back.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：此時天子在長安，曹公尚未秉政。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: at this time the Son of Heaven was at Chang'an, Lord Cao had not yet grasped the government.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the emperor was still in Chang'an and Cao Cao had not yet held the capital.

sentences.zh: 罷兵之詔，不得由曹氏出。〉

translations.literal: An order to disband troops could not have issued from the Cao clan.〉
translations.idiomatic: No such disbandment edict could have come from the Caos alone.〉

sentences.zh: 興平元年，復東征，略定琅邪、東海諸縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingping, he again campaigned east, raiding and pacifying the counties of Langya and Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingping 1 (194) he drove east again, sweeping Langya and Donghai.

sentences.zh: 謙恐，欲走歸丹楊。

translations.literal: Qian was afraid and wished to flee home to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian planned flight to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 會張邈叛迎呂布，太祖還擊布。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Miao rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu; the Grand Progenitor returned to strike Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Miao turned traitor for Lü Bu, and Cao Cao wheeled west to fight him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，謙病死。

translations.literal: In this year Qian died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Qian died of sickness.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：謙死時，年六十三，張昭等爲之哀辭曰：「猗歟使君，君侯將軍，膺秉懿德，允武允文，體足剛直，守以溫仁。

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu says: When Qian died he was sixty-three; Zhang Zhao and others for him made a dirge, saying: "Ah, lord governor, lord general, you bore fine virtue, truly martial, truly civil; your substance was wholly sternly upright, guarded with warm benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu: at sixty-three he died; Zhang Zhao's dirge sang of his virtue, martial and civil, stern yet kind.

sentences.zh: 令舒及盧，遺愛于民；

translations.literal: In orders to Shu and Lu you left kindness among the people;
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Shu and Lu you left love behind;

sentences.zh: 牧幽曁徐，甘棠是均。

translations.literal: shepherding You and then Xu, the sweet pear was even for all.
translations.idiomatic: as governor of You and Xu you were fair as the pear-tree shade.

sentences.zh: 憬憬夷貊，賴侯以清；

translations.literal: The distant Yi and Mo relied on you, lord, to be cleared;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tribes stilled by your hand;

sentences.zh: 蠢蠢妖寇，匪侯不寧。

translations.literal: the wriggling demon bandits—without you, lord, they were not quieted.
translations.idiomatic: rebellious vermin—without you they would not rest.

sentences.zh: 唯帝念績，爵命以章，旣牧且侯，啟土溧陽。

translations.literal: Only the emperor remembered your deeds; rank and mandate made them splendid; you were both shepherd and marquis, opening soil at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne remembered your service, enfeoffed you at Liyang, shepherd and lord.

sentences.zh: 遂升上將，受號安東，將平世難，社稷是崇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rose to supreme general, receiving the title who pacifies the east; he was about to settle the age's troubles and exalt the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who pacifies the east to heal the age and guard the state.

sentences.zh: 降年不永，奄忽殂薨，喪覆失恃，民知困窮。

translations.literal: The years granted were not long; suddenly he passed away; the roof collapsed and support was lost; the people knew hardship and want.
translations.idiomatic: He died too soon; the people lost their prop and fell into want.

sentences.zh: 曾不旬日，五郡潰崩，哀我人斯，將誰仰憑？

translations.literal: In less than ten days the five commanderies collapsed in ruin; alas for us men—whom shall we look up to rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Within days five commanderies crumbled—whom now shall we lean on?

sentences.zh: 追思靡及，仰叫皇穹。

translations.literal: Pursuing thought cannot reach him; we look up and cry to vast Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Memory cannot call him back; we lift our cries to heaven.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the grief!

sentences.zh: 」謙二子：商、應，皆不仕。〉

translations.literal: 」Qian had two sons: Shang and Ying; both did not take office.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」He left two sons, Shang and Ying, who never served.〉

sentences.zh: 張楊字稚叔，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, courtesy name Zhishu, was a man of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, courtesy Zhishu, came from Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 以武勇給并州，為武猛從事。

translations.literal: For martial courage he was assigned to Bingzhou and became valorous martial clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His valor won him a post on Bingzhou staff as valorous martial clerk.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，天下亂，帝以所寵小黃門蹇碩為西園上軍校尉，軍京都，欲以御四方，徵天下豪傑以為偏裨。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling's reign the empire was in disorder; the emperor made the favored junior yellow gate Jian Shuo colonel of the western garden upper army, encamped at the capital, wishing thereby to control the four quarters, and summoned heroes of the empire to be wing and flank commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Ling's reign the court named the eunuch Jian Shuo colonel of the western garden host at the capital to overawe the regions and draft empire-wide captains.

sentences.zh: 太祖及袁紹等皆為校尉，屬之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao and others all became colonels and were subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, Yuan Shao, and the rest were made colonels under him.

sentences.zh: 〈《靈帝紀》曰：以虎賁中郎將袁紹為中軍校尉，屯騎校尉鮑鴻為下軍校尉，議郎曹操為典軍校尉，趙融、馮芳為助軍校尉，夏牟、淳于瓊為左右校尉。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Ling says: He appointed Yuan Shao of the tiger brave guard as colonel of the center army, Bao Hong of the mounted camp as colonel of the lower army, Cao Cao, gentleman consultant, as colonel who manages the army, Zhao Rong and Feng Fang as colonels who assist the army, Xia Mou and Chunyu Qiong as colonels of the left and right.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Ling's annals list the eight colonels of the western garden.〉

sentences.zh: 并州刺史丁原遣楊將兵詣碩，為假司馬。

translations.literal: The governor of Bingzhou Ding Yuan sent Yang leading troops to Shuo as acting major.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ding Yuan sent Yang to Jian Shuo with troops as acting major.

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，碩為何進所殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling collapsed; Shuo was killed by He Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Ling died, He Jin killed Jian Shuo.

sentences.zh: 楊復為進所遣，歸本州募兵，得千餘人，因留上黨，擊山賊。

translations.literal: Yang again was dispatched by Jin, returned to his home province to recruit soldiers, obtained more than a thousand men, therefore stayed in Shangdang and attacked mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin sent him home to raise troops; he gathered a thousand men, stayed in Shangdang, and fought hill bandits.

sentences.zh: 進敗，董卓作亂。

translations.literal: Jin was defeated; Dong Zhuo made rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin fell and Dong Zhuo seized power.

sentences.zh: 楊遂以所將攻上黨太守於壺關，不下，略諸縣，眾至數千人。

translations.literal: Yang thereupon with those he led attacked the governor of Shangdang at Huguan, did not take it, raided the various counties, and the host reached several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yang struck the Shangdang governor at Huguan, failed, pillaged counties, and swelled to thousands.

sentences.zh: 山東兵起，欲誅卓。

translations.literal: East of the mountains troops rose, wishing to execute Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern coalition rose to kill Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 袁紹至河內，楊與紹合，復與匈奴單于於夫羅屯漳水。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao reached Henei; Yang joined with Shao, again with the Xiongnu chanyu Yufuluo camped at the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Shao entered Henei; Yang joined him and the chanyu Yufuluo on the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 單于欲叛，紹、楊不從。

translations.literal: The chanyu wished to rebel; Shao and Yang would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu plotted mutiny; Shao and Yang refused.

sentences.zh: 單于執楊與俱去，紹使將麴義追擊於鄴南，破之。

translations.literal: The chanyu seized Yang and went off with him together; Shao ordered the general Qu Yi to pursue and strike south of Ye and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu kidnapped Yang; Shao sent Qu Yi to rout him south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 單于執楊至黎陽，攻破度遼將軍耿祉軍，眾復振。

translations.literal: The chanyu seized Yang and reached Liyang, broke and defeated the army of General Who Crosses Liao Geng Zhi, and the host again recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang the chanyu smashed Geng Zhi's column and Yang's following revived.

sentences.zh: 卓以楊為建義將軍、河內太守。

translations.literal: Zhuo appointed Yang general who establishes righteousness and governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo named him general who establishes righteousness and governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 公孫度

translations.literal: Gongsun Du.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du.

sentences.zh: 公孫度字升濟，本遼東襄平人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Du, courtesy name Shengji, was originally a man of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du, courtesy Shengji, was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 度父延，避吏居玄菟，任度為郡吏。

translations.literal: Du's father Yan, fleeing clerks, dwelt in Xuantu and appointed Du commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan fled official trouble to Xuantu and got Du a clerkship.

sentences.zh: 時玄菟太守公孫琙，子豹，年十八歲，早死。

translations.literal: At the time the governor of Xuantu Gongsun Yu had a son Bao who at eighteen sui died early.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Gongsun Yu of Xuantu had lost a son Bao at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 度少時名豹，又與琙子同年，琙見而親愛之，遣就師學，為取妻。

translations.literal: Du in youth had been named Bao, and was also the same birth year as Yu's son; Yu saw him and loved him dearly, sent him to study under a teacher, and took a wife for him.
translations.idiomatic: Du had shared the childhood name Bao and the same birth year as the dead boy; Yu doted on him, paid for his schooling, and found him a wife.

sentences.zh: 後舉有道，除尚書郎，稍遷冀州刺史，以謠言免。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended possessed of the Way, appointed gentleman of the masters of writing, gradually promoted governor of Jizhou, and removed because of rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended "possessed of the Way," he rose to masters-of-writing gentleman, then Jizhou governor, until slander ousted him.

sentences.zh: 同郡徐榮為董卓中郎將，薦度為遼東太守。

translations.literal: Xu Rong of the same commandery was colonel of the house of Dong Zhuo and recommended Du as governor of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Xu Rong, colonel under Zhuo, nominated him for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 度起玄菟小吏，為遼東郡所輕。

translations.literal: Du rose from a petty clerk of Xuantu and was despised by Liaodong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A lowborn Xuantu clerk, he was sneered at in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 先時，屬國公孫昭守襄平令，召度子康為伍長。

translations.literal: Earlier the dependent state Gongsun Zhao had been defending as magistrate of Xiangping and summoned Du's son Kang as squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zhao of the dependent state, as magistrate of Xiangping, had made Du's son Kang a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 度到官，收昭，笞殺於襄平市。

translations.literal: When Du reached office, he seized Zhao, flogged him to death in the market of Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Du took office, arrested Zhao, and had him flogged to death in Xiangping market.

sentences.zh: 郡中名豪大姓田韶等宿遇無恩，皆以法誅，所夷滅百餘家，郡中震栗。

translations.literal: Noted magnates and great surnames of the commandery such as Tian Shao, who in the past had shown him no kindness, he all executed by law; those exterminated were more than a hundred households; the commandery trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Great families who had slighted him—over a hundred clans—were wiped out by law until the commandery shook.

sentences.zh: 東伐高句驪，西擊烏丸，威行海外。

translations.literal: He campaigned east against Gaogouli, struck west the Wuhuan, and his awe reached beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Koguryŏ east and Wuhuan west until his name carried overseas.

sentences.zh: 十二年，太祖征三郡烏丸，屠柳城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Grand Progenitor campaigned against the Wuhuan of three commanderies and slaughtered Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (207) Cao Cao attacked the three Wuhuan states and sacked Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 袁尚等奔遼東，康斬送尚首。

translations.literal: Yuan Shang and others fled to Liaodong; Kang beheaded them and sent Shang's head.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang fled east; Kang cut off his head for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 語在武紀。

translations.literal: The language is in the martial annals.
translations.idiomatic: The story is told in the martial annals.

sentences.zh: 封康襄平侯，拜左將軍。

translations.literal: Kang was enfeoffed marquis of Xiangping and appointed general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was enfeoffed marquis of Xiangping and named general of the left.

sentences.zh: 康死，子晃、淵等皆小，眾立恭為遼東太守。

translations.literal: When Kang died, his sons Huang and Yuan and others were all small; the host established Gong as governor of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's sons were infants; the gentry set Gong Yang as governor.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，遣使即拜恭為車騎將軍、假節，封平郭侯；

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he sent envoys to appoint Gong at once general of chariots and cavalry, credential-bearing, enfeoffed marquis of Pingguo;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen confirmed Gong as general of chariots and cavalry with credentials and marquis of Pingguo;

sentences.zh: 追贈康大司馬。

translations.literal: posthumously enfeoffed Kang grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: he posthumously named Kang grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 公孫淵

translations.literal: Gongsun Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan.

sentences.zh: 初，恭病陰消為閹人，劣弱不能治國。

translations.literal: At first, when Gong was ill his privates wasted away so that he became a eunuch; feeble and weak, he could not govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gong wasted away from an illness that unmanned him; too frail to govern, he lost real control of the province.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，淵脅奪恭位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Yuan coerced and seized Gong's position.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 (228) Yuan seized Gong's seat by force.

sentences.zh: 明帝即

translations.literal: Upon Emperor Ming's accession
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne,

translations.literal: (The manuscript adds the graph wei meaning "throne.")
translations.idiomatic: (A gloss inserts the missing word for "throne.")

sentences.zh: 拜淵揚烈將軍、遼東太守。

translations.literal: Yuan was appointed general who displays fierceness and governor of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Yuan general who displays fierceness and governor of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 淵遣使南通孫權，往來賂遺。

translations.literal: Yuan sent envoys south to communicate with Sun Quan, going back and forth with bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan opened talks with Sun Quan south of the Yangzi, sending gifts both ways.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》載淵表權曰：

translations.literal: 〈The Wushu records Yuan's memorial to Quan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wushu preserves his memorial to Quan:

sentences.zh: 臣伏惟遭天地反易，遇無妄之運；

translations.literal: Your subject prostrate considers that I have encountered heaven and earth turned upside down, met the fortune of "no error" reversed;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that heaven and earth are overturned and I stand in perilous times;

sentences.zh: 王路未夷，傾側擾攘。

translations.literal: The kingly way is not yet level; the realm tilts and is turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: The royal road is still blocked and the realm reels.

sentences.zh: 自先人以來，歷事漢、魏，階緣際會，為國效節，繼世享任，得守籓表，猶知符命未有攸歸。

translations.literal: From the ancestors onward we have served Han and Wei in succession, climbed by fortunate meetings, rendered loyalty to the state, enjoyed office generation after generation, been able to guard the outer screen, and still know that the tally-mandate has not yet found its resting place.
translations.idiomatic: For generations we have served Han and then Wei, risen by chance, guarded the frontier, and known the mandate of rule was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 每感厚恩，頻辱顯使，退念人臣交不越境，是以固守所執，拒違前使。

translations.literal: Each time I feel your deep kindness and repeatedly am shamed by eminent envoys; turning back I reflect that a minister's dealings do not cross borders—therefore I firmly hold what I grasp and have refused your former messengers.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace has reached us often, yet a subject may not traffic beyond his border—so I held my ground and turned earlier embassies away.

sentences.zh: 雖義無二信，敢忘大恩！

translations.literal: Although in righteousness there is no second loyalty, how dare I forget the great grace!
translations.idiomatic: Duty allows but one allegiance—still I have not forgotten your kindness.

sentences.zh: 陛下鎮撫，長存小國，前後裴校尉、葛都尉等到，奉被敕誡，聖旨彌密，重紈累素，幽明備著，所以申示之事，言提其耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pacifies and consoles, long preserving our small state; before and after Colonel Pei, Commandant Ge, and others arrived, bearing received admonitions—your holy purpose grew ever more intimate, layer on layer of white silk, dark and bright fully set forth—therefore the matters you declared were spoken as if tugging my ear.
translations.idiomatic: You have long shielded our small domain; envoys brought ever clearer edicts, written in repeated silks, until your meaning rang in my ears.

sentences.zh: 臣晝則謳吟，宵則發夢，終身誦之，志不知足。

translations.literal: Your subject by day then chants and intones, by night then dreams awake; all my life I recite it, my intent never knowing satiety.
translations.idiomatic: I murmur your words by day and dream them by night, never sated with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 季末凶荒，乾坤否塞，兵革未戢，人民盪析。

translations.literal: In the evil tail of the age there is famine; heaven and earth are blocked; arms are not yet stilled; the people are scattered and broken.
translations.idiomatic: These last evil years have blocked heaven and earth, left arms unstacked, and scattered the people.

sentences.zh: 仰此天命將有眷顧，私從一隅永瞻雲日。

translations.literal: Looking up to this, Heaven's mandate will show favor; privately from one corner I forever gaze at cloud and sun.
translations.idiomatic: I trust Heaven will smile again; from this distant corner I still face the light of the throne.

sentences.zh: 今魏家不能採錄忠善，褒功臣之後，乃令讒訛得行其志，聽幽州刺史、東萊太守誑誤之言，猥興州兵，圖害臣郡。

translations.literal: Now the house of Wei cannot gather and record the loyal and good, praise the descendants of meritorious servants, but lets slander run its course, heeds the deceitful words of the governor of Youzhou and the governor of Donglai, rashly raises provincial troops, and plots harm against my commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei will not honor loyalty; calumniators sway the court; Youzhou and Donglai whisper lies—now provincial armies march against my district.

sentences.zh: 臣不負魏，而魏絕之。

translations.literal: Your subject has not betrayed Wei, yet Wei cuts me off.
translations.idiomatic: I have not betrayed Wei; Wei has betrayed me.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞人臣有去就之分；

translations.literal: I have heard that among human ministers there is the principle of staying or leaving;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers may serve or quit—so the classics say;

sentences.zh: 田饒適齊，樂毅走趙，以不得事主，故保有道之君；

translations.literal: Tian Rao went to Qi, Yue Yi fled to Zhao, because they could not obtain a lord to serve, therefore they kept to a lord possessed of the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rao fled to Qi, Yue Yi to Zhao, when they could not serve upright rulers;

sentences.zh: 陳平、耿況，亦睹時變，卒歸於漢，勒名帝籍。

translations.literal: Chen Ping and Geng Kuang also watched the times change and in the end returned to Han, inscribing their names on the imperial rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping and Geng Kuang read the times and ended in Han service, their names carved on the roster of merit.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德不再出，時不世遇，是以慺慺懷慕自納，望遠視險，有如近易。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself: your Majesty's virtue does not come twice; the time is not met once in an age; therefore trembling I cherish admiration and offer myself, gazing at the distance and seeing peril as if it were near and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue is unique; this moment will not come again—so I tremble with awe and draw near, though the road seems perilous as plain ground.

sentences.zh: 誠原神謨蚤定洪業，奮六師之勢，收河、洛之地，為聖代宗。

translations.literal: Truly I pray your divine plan will soon settle the great enterprise, rouse the power of the six hosts, recover the lands of He and Luo, and be the ancestor of this sage age.
translations.idiomatic: May you soon rouse the hosts, reclaim the Yellow and Luo heartland, and stand as founder of a new age.

sentences.zh: 天下幸甚！

translations.literal: The empire will be supremely fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Then all under Heaven will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：國家知淵兩端，而恐遼東吏民為淵所誤。

translations.literal: The Weilüe says: The state knew Yuan played both ends and feared the officials and people of Liaodong might be misled by Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilüe notes that Wei knew Yuan was double-dealing and feared Liaodong might follow him astray.

sentences.zh: 故公文下遼東，因赦之曰：

translations.literal: Therefore a public document went down to Liaodong, and by amnesty it said:
translations.idiomatic: So Wei sent an open letter south with this amnesty:

sentences.zh: 告遼東、玄菟將校吏民：逆賊孫權遭遇亂階，因其先人劫略州郡，遂成群凶，自擅江表，含垢藏疾。

translations.literal: We declare to the generals, clerks, and people of Liaodong and Xuantu: the rebel Sun Quan encountered a time of chaos; relying on his forebears he plundered provinces and commanderies, thereupon became a pack of villains, himself occupying the lands south of the Yangzi, harboring filth and concealing sickness.
translations.idiomatic: To officers and folk of Liaodong and Xuantu: Sun Quan is a rebel who rode chaos, followed bandit forbears, seized the southland, and nursed every crime in secret.

sentences.zh: 冀其可化，故割地王權，使南面稱孤，位以上將，禮以九命。

translations.literal: We hoped he might be transformed; therefore we carved out land and made Quan king, letting him face south as sovereign and take the ruler's humble style, rank him as supreme general, and treat him with the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: We hoped to reform him—ceded him territory, kingship south of the river with full royal ritual, supreme generalship, and the nine ritual gifts.

sentences.zh: 權親叉手，北向稽顙。

translations.literal: Quan personally folded his hands and kowtowed toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Quan clasped his hands and kowtowed toward the northern court.

sentences.zh: 假人臣之寵，受人臣之榮，未有如權者也。

translations.literal: To borrow a subject's favor and receive a subject's glory—none has been like Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Never has a vassal enjoyed such favor and such glory as Quan.

sentences.zh: 狼子野心，告令難移，卒歸反覆，背恩叛主，滔天逆神，乃敢僭號。

translations.literal: A wolf cub's wild heart—warnings cannot move him; in the end he turned again and again, betrayed grace and rebelled against his lord, offended heaven and reversed the gods, and dared usurp the supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: He proved a wolf with a wolf's heart, spurned every warning, betrayed his sovereign, outraged Heaven, and seized an emperor's style.

sentences.zh: 恃江湖之險阻，王誅未加。

translations.literal: He relies on the Yangzi's barriers; royal punishment has not yet been applied.
translations.idiomatic: River ramparts have shielded him from the axe—until now.

sentences.zh: 比年已來，复遠遣船，越渡大海，多持貨物，誑誘邊民。

translations.literal: In recent years again he has far dispatched ships, crossed the great sea, carrying much goods, to deceive and entice border people.
translations.idiomatic: Lately he sends fleets across the sea with goods to seduce our frontier.

sentences.zh: 邊民無知，與之交關。

translations.literal: The border people, ignorant, have dealings with them.
translations.idiomatic: Ignorant borderers trade with him.

sentences.zh: 長吏以下，莫肯禁止。

translations.literal: From chief clerks downward none was willing to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Local officers let it pass.

sentences.zh: 至使周賀浮舟百艘，沈滯津岸，貿遷有無。

translations.literal: To the point that Zhou He floated a hundred boats, lay stalled at the ford, and bartered have and want.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou He brought a hundred hulls to the Ta ford and opened a market.

sentences.zh: 既不疑拒，齎以名馬，又使宿舒隨賀通好。

translations.literal: You neither doubted nor refused him, supplied him with famous horses, and also sent Su Shu with He to open good relations.
translations.idiomatic: You never stopped him—you sent fine horses and let Su Shu sail with him to seal friendship.

sentences.zh: 十室之邑，猶有忠信，陷君於惡，春秋所書也。

translations.literal: In a hamlet of ten houses there are still loyalty and good faith; to trap your lord in evil is what the Spring and Autumn records.
translations.idiomatic: Even a village keeps faith; leading your prince into crime is what the Chunqiu condemns.

sentences.zh: 今遼東、玄菟奉事國朝，紆青拖紫，以千百為數，戴纚垂纓，咸佩印綬，曾無匡正納善之言。

translations.literal: Now Liaodong and Xuantu serve the court of the state, trail cyan and purple sashes by the hundreds and thousands, wear tall caps with dangling tassels, all girded with seals and ribbons—yet never a word to correct the ruler or offer good counsel.
translations.idiomatic: You wear court rank by the thousand yet never spoke truth to power.

sentences.zh: 龜玉毀於櫝，虎兕出於匣，是誰之過歟？

translations.literal: The tortoise and jade are destroyed in the casket; the tiger and rhinoceros come out of the box—whose fault is it?
translations.idiomatic: When the casket breaks the gems shatter—whose fault is the beast's escape?

sentences.zh: 國朝為子大夫羞之！

translations.literal: The state is ashamed for you, great officers!
translations.idiomatic: The court blushes for you, gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 昔狐突有言：『父教子貳，何以事君？

translations.literal: Formerly Hu Tu had a saying: "If the father teaches the son twofold loyalty, how shall he serve his lord?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tu said, "A father who teaches divided loyalty unfit his son for service;

sentences.zh: 策名委質，貳乃辟也。

translations.literal: Inscribing the name and pledging the body—twofold loyalty is crime."
translations.idiomatic: once a name is pledged to a lord, double dealing is treason."

sentences.zh: 』今乃阿順邪謀，脅從姦惑，豈獨父兄之教不詳，子弟之舉習非而已哉！

translations.literal: 」Now you fawn on wicked plots and are coerced to follow knavish delusion—is it only that fathers and elder brothers' teaching was not detailed and sons and younger brothers' habits were wrong!
translations.idiomatic: 」Yet you abet treason—do not blame only bad upbringing or youthful habit!

sentences.zh: 若苗穢害田，隨風烈火，芝艾俱焚，安能白別乎？

translations.literal: It is like weeds harming the field: following the wind a fierce fire burns, sweet zhi and wormwood alike are consumed—how can white be told apart?
translations.idiomatic: When the field burns, weed and crop perish together—who can tell guilt from innocence?

sentences.zh: 且又此事固然易見，不及鑑古成敗，書傳所載也。

translations.literal: Moreover this affair is plainly easy to see, not reaching to mirror antiquity's success and failure—it is what books and transmissions record.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson is plain in every history book.

sentences.zh: 江南海北有萬里之限，遼東君臣無怵惕之患，利則義所不利，貴則義所不貴，此為厭安樂之居，求危亡之禍，賤忠貞之節，重背叛之名。

translations.literal: South of the river and north of the sea there is a limit of ten thousand li; lord and ministers of Liaodong have no alarm of peril; where profit is what righteousness counts not profitable, where honor is what righteousness counts not honorable—this is to weary of peaceful dwelling, seek the disaster of destruction, despise the integrity of loyalty and uprightness, and prize the name of betrayal.
translations.idiomatic: You dwell in peace yet chase profit across a sea that divides you from us—cheapening honor and courting ruin.

sentences.zh: 蠻、貊之長，猶知愛禮，以此事人，亦難為顏！

translations.literal: Even chiefs of Man and Mo know to cherish ritual; with such conduct toward others, how can you show a face!
translations.idiomatic: Even barbarian chiefs honor rite—how can you meet the world's eyes?

sentences.zh: 且又宿舒無罪，擠使入吳，奉不義之使，始與家訣，涕泣而行。

translations.literal: Moreover Su Shu was without crime; you crowded him off to Wu on an unrighteous mission; at first he took leave of his family, weeping as he went.
translations.idiomatic: You thrust guiltless Su Shu east on a shameful errand—he bade his kin farewell in tears.

sentences.zh: 及至賀死之日，覆眾成山，舒雖脫死，魂魄離身。

translations.literal: When it reached the day He died, the overturned host made a mountain; although Shu escaped death, his soul left his body.
translations.idiomatic: When He perished, corpses piled like hills; Shu lived, yet his spirit fled.

sentences.zh: 何所逼迫，乃至於此！

translations.literal: What compulsion drove matters to this pass!
translations.idiomatic: What force could drive men so far?

sentences.zh: 今忠臣烈將，咸忿遼東反覆攜貳，皆欲乘桴浮海，期於肆意。

translations.literal: Now loyal ministers and fierce generals all resent Liaodong's repeated shifting and divided loyalty and all wish to ride rafts across the sea, expecting thereby to indulge their will.
translations.idiomatic: Every loyal captain wants to raft across the strait to punish your wavering.

sentences.zh: 朕為天下父母，加念天下新定，既不欲勞動干戈，遠涉大川，費役如彼，又悼邊陲遺餘黎民，迷誤如此，故遣郎中衛慎、邵瑁等且先奉詔示意。

translations.literal: We, as parents of the empire, moreover think on the empire newly settled; we neither wish to trouble spear and shield nor cross the great streams at such cost in labor; we also grieve that the remaining black-haired people on the borders, misled thus, therefore send gentlemen of the interior Wei Shen and Shao Mao and others for now to bear the edict and show our intent.
translations.idiomatic: We are father and mother to the realm, loath to stir another great war, yet pity you border folk—so we dispatch Wei Shen and Shao Mao to explain our will.

sentences.zh: 若股肱忠良能效節立信以輔時君，反邪就正以建大功，福莫大焉。

translations.literal: If arms and legs, loyal and good, can display integrity and establish trust to aid the lord of the hour, turn from evil to correctness and thereby establish great merit, there is no fortune greater.
translations.idiomatic: Return to righteousness, aid your rightful lord, and earn the greatest blessing.

sentences.zh: 儻恐自嫌已為惡逆所見染汙，不敢倡言，永懷伊戚。

translations.literal: If you fear that having been stained by sight of wicked rebellion you dare not speak first and forever harbor this sorrow,
translations.idiomatic: If shame for past contact with rebels seals your lips,

sentences.zh: 其諸與賊使交通，皆赦除之，與之更始。

translations.literal: all who had traffic with the bandit envoys are pardoned and cleared, and given a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: we pardon every man who dealt with Wu and grant a clean slate.

sentences.zh: 權遣使張彌、許晏等，齎金玉珍寶，立淵為燕王。

translations.literal: Quan sent envoys Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, and others, bearing gold, jade, and precious goods, to establish Yuan as king of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dispatched Zhang Mi and Xu Yan with treasure to crown Yuan king of Yan.

sentences.zh: 淵亦恐權遠不可恃，且貪貨物，誘致其使，悉斬送彌、晏等首，

translations.literal: Yuan also feared Quan was too far to rely on and moreover coveted the goods; he enticed his envoys in, beheaded them all, and sent the heads of Mi, Yan, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan distrusted the distant ally, coveted the gifts, lured the embassy in, and sent their heads back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載淵表曰：

translations.literal: 〈The Weilüe records Yuan's memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe quotes Yuan's memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣前遣校尉宿舒、郎中令孫綜，甘言厚禮，以誘吳賊。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier sent Colonel Su Shu and chief of the gentlemen of the household Sun Zong with sweet words and rich gifts to entice the Wu bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I sent Su Shu and Sun Zong east with honeyed words and lavish gifts to bait Wu.

sentences.zh: 幸賴天道福助大魏，使此賊虜暗然迷惑，違戾群下，不從眾諫，承信臣言，遠遣船使，多將士卒，來致封拜。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on the Way of Heaven blessing and aiding great Wei, it made these bandit captives dimly deluded, rebel against their subordinates, not follow the crowd's remonstrance, trust your subject's words, far dispatch ship envoys, bring many officers and soldiers, and come to deliver investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored Wei: Wu grew reckless, spurned counsel, believed me, and sent a great embassy with troops to seal the sham kingship.

sentences.zh: 臣之所執，得如本志，雖憂罪釁，私懷幸甚。

translations.literal: What your subject held to matched my original intent; although I worry over crime and offense, privately I am greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: My plan worked as I hoped; though I risk blame, I rejoice inwardly.

sentences.zh: 賊眾本號萬人，舒、綜伺察，可七八千人，到沓津。

translations.literal: The bandit host was originally titled ten thousand men; Shu and Zong reconnoitered that they could be seven or eight thousand, and they reached Ta ford.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed ten thousand men; Shu counted seven or eight thousand at Ta ford.

sentences.zh: 偽使者張彌、許晏與中郎將萬泰、校尉裴潛將吏兵四百餘人，齎文書命服什物，下到臣郡。

translations.literal: The false envoys Zhang Mi and Xu Yan with colonel of the gentlemen of the household Wan Tai and colonel Pei Qian led more than four hundred officers and soldiers, bearing documents, mandated robes, and gear, and came down to your subject's commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, Wan Tai, and Pei Qian landed with four hundred men, regalia, and patents.

sentences.zh: 泰、潛別齎致遺貨物，欲因市馬。

translations.literal: Tai and Qian separately also brought goods sent as gifts, wishing thereby to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and Qian brought extra goods to trade for horses.

sentences.zh: 軍將賀達、虞諮領餘眾在船所。

translations.literal: The generals He Da and Yu Zi led the remaining host at the ships.
translations.idiomatic: He Da and Yu Zi waited aboard with the rest.

sentences.zh: 臣本欲須涼節乃取彌等，而彌等人兵眾多，見臣不便承受吳命，意有猜疑。

translations.literal: Your subject originally wished to wait for the cool season then seize Mi and others, but Mi and others had many troops and men, saw that your subject was not convenient to accept Wu's command, and their intentions harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to wait for cool weather to strike, but their numbers were large, saw I would not kneel to Wu, and grew wary.

sentences.zh: 懼其先作，變態妄生，即進兵圍取，斬彌、晏、泰、潛等首級。

translations.literal: Fearing they would act first and strange changes rashly arise, I immediately advanced troops, surrounded and took them, and beheaded Mi, Yan, Tai, Qian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a coup, I surrounded them at once and took Mi, Yan, Tai, and Qian's heads.

sentences.zh: 其吏從兵眾，皆士伍小人，給使東西，不得自由，面縛乞降，不忍誅殺，輒聽納受，徙充邊城。

translations.literal: Their clerks and following soldiers were all common privates, supplied to run east and west without freedom of their own; bound hand before face they begged to surrender; I could not bear to execute and kill them, thereupon listened and accepted them, moved them to fill the border cities.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers were common soldiers; I spared the bound men who yielded and sent them to the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 別遣將韓起等率將三軍，馳行至沓。

translations.literal: Separately I dispatched the general Han Qi and others to lead the three armies and gallop to reach Ta.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Han Qi with the three hosts at full gallop for Ta.

sentences.zh: 使領長史柳遠設賓主禮誘請達、諮，三軍潛伏以待其下，又驅群馬貨物，欲與交市。

translations.literal: I ordered chief clerk Liu Yuan to set host-guest rites to entice and invite Da and Zi; the three armies lay in ambush to await their landing; again I drove herds of horses and goods, wishing to trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Liu Yuan played host to lure Da and Zi ashore while ambushers hid; we drove horses forward as if to trade.

sentences.zh: 達、諮懷疑不下，使諸市買者五六百人下，欲交市。

translations.literal: Da and Zi harbored suspicion and did not come down; they sent five or six hundred of the market buyers to come down, wishing to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious, they sent five or six hundred men to the beach to barter.

sentences.zh: 起等金鼓始震，鋒矢亂發，斬首三百餘級，被創赴水沒溺者可二百餘人，其散走山谷，來歸降及藏竄飢餓死者，不在數中。

translations.literal: When Qi and others' drums and gongs first shook, spear points and arrows flew in disorder; more than three hundred heads were cut off; those wounded who rushed into the water and drowned were perhaps more than two hundred; those who scattered into mountain valleys, came to surrender, or hid and starved to death are not counted in the number.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drumstroke our archers volleyed—three hundred heads, two hundred drowned, more lost in the hills uncounted.

sentences.zh: 得銀印、銅印、兵器、資貨，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Silver seals, bronze seals, weapons, and goods taken were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: We captured silver and bronze seals, arms, and loot beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 謹遣西曹掾公孫珩奉送賊權所假臣節、印綬、符策、九錫、什物，及彌等偽節、印綬、首級。

translations.literal: Respectfully I send west-department aide Gongsun Heng to deliver the credentials, seal ribbons, tallies, nine bestowals, and gear that the bandit Quan falsely lent your subject, together with Mi and others' false credentials, seal ribbons, and heads.
translations.idiomatic: I send Gongsun Heng west with Quan's bogus patents, nine honors, regalia, and the envoys' heads.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「宿舒、孫綜前到吳，賊權問臣家內小大，舒、綜對臣有三息，脩別屬亡弟。

translations.literal: 」He also said: "When earlier Su Shu and Sun Zong reached Wu, the bandit Quan asked about your subject's family great and small; Shu and Zong answered that your subject had three sons, Xiu being separately attached to a deceased younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "When Shu and Zong reached Wu, Quan asked after my household; they said I had three sons, naming Xiu as heir to a dead brother.

sentences.zh: 權敢姦巧，便擅拜命。

translations.literal: Quan dared knavish trickery and on his own presumed to issue appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then played the fool and presumed to invest me.

sentences.zh: 謹封送印綬、符策。

translations.literal: Respectfully I seal and send the seal ribbons and tallies.
translations.idiomatic: I seal and forward his counterfeit seals and tallies.

sentences.zh: 臣雖無昔人洗耳之風，慚為賊權汙損所加，既行天誅，猶有餘忿。」

translations.literal: Your subject although without the wind of the ancients who washed their ears, am ashamed by what the bandit Quan defiled and added; since I have executed Heaven's punishment, still there remains surplus anger."
translations.idiomatic: I lack the sage who washed his ears to flee office, yet I burn with shame at Quan's insult—even after heaven's stroke the embers of rage remain."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣父康，昔殺權使，結為讎隙。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject's father Kang in the past killed Quan's envoy and knotted enmity.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "My father Kang slew Wu's envoy and made a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 今乃譎欺，遺使誘致，令權傾心，虛國竭祿，遠命上卿，寵授極位，震動南土，備盡禮數。

translations.literal: Now he deceives and cheats, sends envoys to lure him in, makes Quan pour out his heart, empties the state and exhausts its revenue, far orders a senior minister, favors and invests the utmost rank, shakes the southern lands, exhausts every ritual number.
translations.idiomatic: Now Quan empties his treasury, sends a high minister, heaps the highest honors, and shakes the south with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又權待舒、綜，契委曲，君臣上下，畢歡竭情。

translations.literal: Moreover Quan toward Shu and Zong was intimate in every twist; lord and minister, high and low, exhausted joy and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted Shu and Zong as honored kin, lord and ministers at one table.

sentences.zh: 而令四使見殺，梟示萬里，士眾流離，屠戮津渚，慚恥遠布，痛辱彌天。

translations.literal: Yet he made four envoys be killed and their heads displayed for ten thousand li; soldiers and hosts drifted apart, were slaughtered at the ford shallows; shame spread far, agony and insult filled heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Then I killed his four envoys, exposed their heads, slaughtered his men at the landing—humiliation that fills the sky.

sentences.zh: 權之怨疾，將刻肌骨。

translations.literal: Quan's resentment and hatred will carve into muscle and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Quan will hate me to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 若天衰其業，使至喪隕，權將內傷憤激而死。

translations.literal: If Heaven weakens his enterprise and lets him meet sudden ruin, Quan will die of inward wound and furious shock.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven ends him soon, rage will burst his heart.

sentences.zh: 若期運未訖，將播毒螫，必恐長虵來為寇害。

translations.literal: If the allotted span is not yet finished, he will spread venomous sting; I surely fear the long serpent will come as bandit harm.
translations.idiomatic: If he lives on, his sting will reach us—I fear the long snake will strike as raider.

sentences.zh: 徐州諸屯及城陽諸郡，與相接近，如有船眾後年向海門，得其消息，乞速告臣，使得備豫。」

translations.literal: The various garrisons of Xuzhou and the commanderies of Chengyang and others border him closely; if there are ship hosts in later years heading toward the sea gate, obtaining their news, I beg you quickly to inform your subject, enabling me to prepare in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou and Chengyang lie nearest Wu; if next year you hear of fleets bound for our seas, warn me at once that I may prepare."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣門戶受恩，實深實重，自臣承攝即事以來，連被榮寵，殊特無量，分當隕越，竭力致死。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject's gates and household have received grace, truly deep, truly heavy; from the time your subject took charge of affairs, repeatedly I have received glory and favor, extraordinary beyond measure; by duty I ought to crumble and exhaust my strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Again: "My house owes Wei boundless favor; since I took office honors have showered on me—I should spend myself to the dust.

sentences.zh: 而臣狂愚，意計迷闇，不即禽賊，以至見疑。

translations.literal: Yet your subject was mad and foolish, plans and reckonings dim and dark, not at once seizing the bandits, thereby coming under suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my slow wit let me delay striking the bandits and drew suspicion.

sentences.zh: 前章表所陳情趣事勢，實但欲罷弊此賊，使困自絕，誠不敢背累世之恩，附僭盜之虜也。

translations.literal: In the memorial and tables submitted before, the feelings, aims, affairs, and situation were truly only wishing to wear out this bandit and make him trapped unto self-extinction; truly I dared not betray the grace of many generations and attach myself to a usurping bandit.
translations.idiomatic: My earlier memorials meant only to exhaust Wu, not to join a rebel—never to betray generations of Wei grace.

sentences.zh: 而後愛憎之人，緣事加誣，偽生節目，卒令明聽疑於市虎，移恩改愛，興動威怒，幾至沈沒，長為負忝。

translations.literal: Afterward those who loved or hated, relying on affairs, added false slander, falsely produced branches and knots, in the end making clear hearing doubt the market tiger, shifting grace and changing love, rousing awesome anger, almost to sinking and drowning, long to be burdened with shame.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers twisted every act until the court saw tigers in the market—my favor nearly drowned in wrath.

sentences.zh: 幸賴慈恩，猶垂三宥，使得補過，解除愆責。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on kindly grace, still extending the three pardons, I was enabled to mend fault and remove the burden of blame.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy thrice spared me and let me atone.

sentences.zh: 如天威遠加，不見假借，早當麋碎，辱先廢祀，何緣自明，建微功。

translations.literal: If heavenly majesty from afar did not show indulgence, long ago I ought to have been ground to fragments, shaming the ancestors and cutting sacrifice—how could I have cleared myself and established slight merit?
translations.idiomatic: Had your wrath struck once, I would be dust and my line ended—how then show this small service?

sentences.zh: 臣既喜於事捷，得自申展，悲於疇昔，至此變故，餘怖踴躍，未敢便寧。

translations.literal: Your subject both rejoices that the affair succeeded and was able to declare himself, and grieves at what happened from former days to this change and disaster; remaining fear leaps within, not daring yet to be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoice in success yet tremble at how far things nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下既崇春日生全之仁，除忿塞隙，抑弭纖介，推今亮往，察臣本心，長令抱戴，銜分三泉。」

translations.literal: Only may your Majesty, since you honor the spring sun's grace that gives life and preserves all, remove anger and stop cracks, suppress and end fine hairs of offense, push the present to light the past, examine your subject's original heart, long let me embrace and bear favor, holding the share even in the three springs."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, who give life like spring sunlight, to seal old cracks, overlook specks of fault, read my heart by this deed, and let me die still wearing your favor."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣被服光榮，恩情未報，而以罪釁，自招譴怒，分當即戮，為眾社戒。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject has worn bright glory; grace and kindness are not yet repaid, yet by crime and offense I have invited stern anger; by allotment I ought at once to be executed as a warning to the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Again: "I wear honors I have not yet repaid; my faults invite execution as a warning to the state.

sentences.zh: 所以越典詭常，偽通於吳，誠自念窮迫，報效未立，而為天威督罰所加，長恐奄忽不得自洗。

translations.literal: Therefore I crossed the norm and deceived the constant, falsely communicated with Wu—truly I thought myself pressed to extremity, merit not yet established, while heavenly majesty's supervision and punishment pressed on me; I always feared sudden death would not let me cleanse myself.
translations.idiomatic: I played false with Wu because I feared your punishment before I could prove loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故敢自闕替廢於一年，遣使誘吳，知其必來，權之求郡，積有年歲，初無倡答一言之應，今權得使，來必不疑，至此一舉，果如所規，上卿大眾，翕赫豐盛，財貨賂遺，傾國極位，到見禽取，流離死亡，千有餘人，滅絕不反。

translations.literal: Therefore I dared to remove and dismiss myself for one year, send envoys to entice Wu, knowing they would surely come; Quan's seeking a commandery had piled up years; at first there was not one word of response; now Quan obtained envoys and was sure to be without doubt; with this one stroke it indeed matched what was planned—senior ministers and great hosts, blazing and abundant, goods and bribes, exhausting the state and utmost rank, arrived and were captured, drifted apart and died, more than a thousand men, extinguished and not returning.
translations.idiomatic: I feigned disgrace a year to bait Wu—Quan had begged a county for years without answer; one embassy lured his great ministers and treasure into our trap; over a thousand perished, none returning.

sentences.zh: 此誠暴猾賊之鋒，摧矜誇之巧，昭示天下，破損其業，足以慚之矣。

translations.literal: This truly is blunting the blade of a violent knave, crushing the trick of boastful pride, making clear to the empire and breaking his enterprise—enough to shame him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I broke his pride and advertised his shame to the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣之慺慺念效於國，雖有非常之過，亦有非常之功，原陛下原其逾闕之愆，採其亳毛之善，使得國恩，保全終始矣。

translations.literal: Your subject's trembling thought of serving the effect to the state, although there are extraordinary faults, also has extraordinary merit; I pray your Majesty forgive the transgression of crossing bounds, gather the goodness of a hair's tip, let me obtain the state's grace and preserve beginning and end."
translations.idiomatic: I have overstepped yet served you—pardon my trespass, credit a hair's worth of good, and let me end my days in your grace."

sentences.zh: 大司馬長史臣郭昕、參軍臣柳浦等七百八十九人言：奉被今年七月己卯詔書，伏讀懇切，精魄散越，不知身命所當投措！

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the grand marshal, your subject Guo Xin, and aide Liu Pu and seven hundred eighty-nine others say: We received this year's seventh month jimao day edict; prostrate, we read it earnest and cutting; essence and soul scatter beyond bounds—we do not know where body and life should be cast!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xin, Liu Pu, and 789 officers write: the seventh-month edict left us soul-scattered, not knowing where to turn.

sentences.zh: 昕等伏自惟省，螻蟻小丑，器非時用，遭值千載，被受公孫淵祖考以來光明之德，惠澤沾渥，滋潤榮華，無寸尺之功，有負乘之累；

translations.literal: Xin and others prostrate themselves and reflect: we are ants and petty clowns, vessels not timely useful; encountering a thousand years, we have received from Gongsun Yuan's ancestors and fathers down the bright virtue, moisture of favor soaking deep, nourishing splendor and glory; we have not merit of an inch or foot, yet bear the burden of riding the worthy while carrying a petty man;
translations.idiomatic: We are mites raised by the Gongsuns' light—no merit, only shame of riding above our station;

sentences.zh: 遂蒙褒獎，登名天府，並以駑蹇附龍託驥，紆青拖紫，飛騰雲梯，感恩惟報，死不擇地。

translations.literal: thereupon we received praise and reward, ascended the name to heaven's treasury, and all with lame slow steps attached to dragon and clung to thoroughbred, trailed cyan and purple, flew up the cloud ladder—thinking on grace we wish only to repay, death not choosing ground.
translations.idiomatic: yet we were raised to the roster, draped in purple, mounted the cloud ladder—we owe deathless debt.
