sentences.zh: 臣等聞明君在上，聽政採言，人臣在下，得無隱情，是以因緣訴讓，冒犯愬冤。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that when an enlightened lord is above, he listens to government and gathers words; when human ministers are below, they may not hide feeling—therefore relying on cause we appeal and complain, offending to state wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Under a wise ruler men may speak—we beg leave to voice our grievance.

sentences.zh: 郡在籓表，密邇不羈，平昔三州，轉輸費調，以供賞賜，歲用累億，虛耗中國。

translations.literal: The commandery is at the outer screen, close to the unruly; in ordinary times the three provinces rotated transport of fees and levies to supply rewards and gifts, yearly expense mounting to hundred millions, vainly exhausting the central states.
translations.idiomatic: Our march is on the rim, cheek by jowl with rebels; for years three provinces shipped tribute costing hundreds of millions to buy peace.

sentences.zh: 然猶跋扈，虔劉邊陲，烽火相望，羽檄相逮，城門晝閉，路無行人，州郡兵戈，奔散覆沒。

translations.literal: Yet still they acted the bully, slaughtered the frontier; beacon fires faced one another; feathered urgency chased one another; city gates were closed by day; there was no traveler on the roads; provincial troops with weapons ran, scattered, overturned, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Still the Gongsuns ravaged the marches—beacons blazed, gates shut by day, armies broke and drowned.

sentences.zh: 淵祖父度初來臨郡，承受荒殘，開日月之光，建神武之略，聚烏合之民，掃地為業，威震燿於殊俗，德澤被於群生。

translations.literal: Yuan's grandfather Du when first coming to the commandery took over waste and ruin, opened the light of sun and moon, set up divine martial strategy, gathered a host like crows united, swept the ground to make enterprise, awe shaking and shining in strange customs, virtuous moisture covering the living masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Du first came he raised order from ruins, gathered rabble into an army, struck awe through the tribes, and spread mercy to the living.

sentences.zh: 遼土之不壞，實度是賴。

translations.literal: That the soil of Liao was not ruined was truly what Du relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong survives today because Du built its foundation.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『微管仲，吾其被髮左衽。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Without Guan Zhong, I would let my hair hang loose and fasten my robe on the left."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Without Guan Zhong we should all be wearing barbarian dress."

sentences.zh: 』向不遭度，則郡早為丘墟，而民系於虜廷矣。

translations.literal: Had we not encountered Du, the commandery would long ago have been mounds and ruins, and the people bound at the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Without Du the district would be rubble and the people slaves to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 遺風餘愛，永存不朽。

translations.literal: The wind he left and the love remaining forever endure imperishable.
translations.idiomatic: His legacy of kindness still lives.

sentences.zh: 度既薨殂，吏民感慕，欣戴子康，尊而奉之。

translations.literal: When Du had passed away, officials and people felt moved admiration, joyfully bore Kang his son, honored and served him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du died the people gladly accepted his son Kang as lord.

sentences.zh: 康踐統洪緒，克壯徽猷，文昭武烈，邁德種仁；

translations.literal: Kang stepped onto the great cord, strengthened fine strategy, civil splendor martial majesty, surpassed virtue and planted benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Kang enlarged his father's design—civil and martial, generous and strong.

sentences.zh: 乃心京輦，翼翼虔恭，佐國平亂，效績紛紜，功隆事大，勳藏王府。

translations.literal: His heart toward the capital precincts, cautious and reverent, aided the state and pacified disorder, merit piled in confusion, work great, feats hidden in the royal treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his heart on Luoyang, served the court loyally, and piled deeds high in the royal archives.

sentences.zh: 度、康當值武皇帝休明之會，合策名之計，夾輔漢室，降身委質，卑己事魏。

translations.literal: Du and Kang met the conjunction of Martial Emperor's enlightened age, joined plans to inscribe their names, aided flank the Han house, lowered their persons and pledged substance, humbled themselves to serve Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They lived under Emperor Wu's bright reign, pledged themselves to Han and then to Wei, and bowed low in service.

sentences.zh: 匪處小厭大，畏而服焉，乃慕託高風，懷仰盛懿也。

translations.literal: It was not that they dwelt on the small and hated the large, feared and submitted—it was that they admired and relied on lofty wind, cherished and looked up to great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They did not cringe before a greater power—they honored true greatness.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝亦虛心接納，待以不次，功無鉅細，每不見忘。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor likewise with empty heart received them, treated them out of sequence, merit whether great or small, each time did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu welcomed them openly and never forgot the least of their service.

sentences.zh: 又命之曰：『海北土地，割以付君，世世子孫，實得有之。

translations.literal: Again he ordered them: "The land north of the sea I cut and give to you; generation after generation of sons and grandsons shall truly possess it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The lands north of the Bohai I give your line to hold forever."

sentences.zh: 』皇天后土，實聞德音。

translations.literal: August Heaven and sovereign earth truly hear this virtuous pronouncement.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth heard that pledge.

sentences.zh: 臣庶小大，豫在下風，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: The host of subjects great and small, beforehand in the lower wind, received it circling, not daring to let it fall.
translations.idiomatic: We who stand below accepted it with trembling care.

sentences.zh: 淵生有蘭石之姿，少含愷悌之訓，允文允武，忠惠且直；

translations.literal: Yuan was born with orchid-and-stone bearing; in youth he held kind and fraternal training; truly civil, truly martial, loyal, kind, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had the stature of a pillar; raised in kindness, he was both scholar and soldier, loyal and straight.

sentences.zh: 生民欽仰，莫弗懷愛。

translations.literal: The living people looked up to him; none did not cherish love.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him.

sentences.zh: 淵纂戎祖考，君臨萬民，為國以禮，淑化流行，獨見先睹，羅結遐方，勤王之義，視險如夷，世載忠亮，不隕厥名。

translations.literal: Yuan continued the martial work of forebears and fathers, lorded over myriad people, for the state used ritual, fair transformation flowing abroad, alone saw beforehand, net bound the distant quarters; duty to aid the king he viewed peril as flat ground; generations bore loyal brightness and did not let his name fall.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled by rite, bound distant tribes, treated the king's call as plain duty, and his house shone with generations of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 孫權慕義，不遠萬里，連年遣使，欲自結援，雖見絕殺，不念舊怨，纖纖往來，求成恩好。

translations.literal: Sun Quan admired righteousness, not grudging ten thousand li, year after year sent envoys, wished himself to knot alliance; although he was rejected and killed, he did not remember old resentment, went back and forth repeatedly, seeking to complete grace and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wooed him for years across the sea; though Yuan once spurned him, Quan still sent envoys again and again begging friendship.

sentences.zh: 淵執節彌固，不為利回，守志匪石，確乎彌堅。

translations.literal: Yuan held his integrity ever firmer, was not turned by profit, guarded his resolve—it was not stone, yet firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan never wavered for bribes—his resolve was harder than stone.

sentences.zh: 猶懼丹心未見保明，乃卑辭厚幣，誘致權使，梟截獻馘，以示無二。

translations.literal: Still he feared his loyal heart was not yet clearly guaranteed; therefore with humble words and thick silks he enticed Quan's envoys, beheaded them and offered the heads, to show he had no second mind.
translations.idiomatic: To prove his faith to Wei he baited Wu's envoys and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 吳雖在遠，水道通利，舉帆便至，無所隔限。

translations.literal: Wu although lies far, water paths run smoothly; raise sail and one reaches—there is no barrier in between.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lies a sail away—no natural barrier divides us.

sentences.zh: 淵不顧敵讎之深，念存人臣之節，絕強吳之歡，昭事魏之心，靈祇明鑑，普天咸聞。

translations.literal: Yuan did not heed how deep the enemy hatred ran; he kept in mind a minister's integrity, cut off mighty Wu's friendship, displayed service to Wei's heart—spirits bright mirror, all within heaven hear.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Wu to show Wei his heart—gods and men could witness it.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘉美洪烈，懿茲武功，誕錫休命，寵亞齊、魯，下及陪臣，普受介福。

translations.literal: Your Majesty praised the great enterprise, honored this martial achievement, broadly granted gracious mandate, favor second only to Qi and Lu, reaching down to attendant ministers, all receiving blessing.
translations.idiomatic: You praised his arms, ennobled his kin like the old dukes of Qi and Lu, and showered favor on his followers.

sentences.zh: 誠以天覆之恩，當卒終始，得竭股肱，永保祿位，不虞一旦，橫被殘酷。

translations.literal: Truly with heaven's covering grace one should see the matter through from start to end, obtain to exhaust arms and thighs, forever preserve salary and rank; who expected in one morning to be struck by cruel violence.
translations.idiomatic: We trusted your favor would last—then sudden ruin struck.

sentences.zh: 惟育養之厚，念積累之效，悲思不遂，痛切見棄，舉國號咷，拊膺泣血。

translations.literal: Only thinking on the thickness of nurture, mindful of piled-up merit, grief that intent was not followed, pain cutting at being cast aside—the whole state wails, beats the breast and weeps blood.
translations.idiomatic: The whole commandery weeps for the nurture he gave and the shame of his fall.

sentences.zh: 夫三軍所伐，蠻夷戎狄，驕逸不虔，於是致武，不聞義國反受誅討。

translations.literal: What the three armies punish are Man, Yi, Rong, and Di—proud and idle, not reverent; thereupon martial power is applied; one does not hear that a righteous state in turn receives execution and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Armies march against wild tribes, not against loyal vassals.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖王之制，五服之域，有不供職，則脩文德，而又不至，然後征伐。

translations.literal: In general the sage king's system: within the domain of the five zones of service, if they do not perform duty, then he cultivates civil virtue; if again they do not arrive, then he campaigns and punishes.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king first teaches; only then does he strike.

sentences.zh: 淵小心翼翼，恪恭於位，勤事奉上，可謂勉矣。

translations.literal: Yuan was cautious and careful, reverently respectful in his post, labored at affairs and served superiors—one may call him diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 盡忠竭節，還被患禍。

translations.literal: He exhausted loyalty and drained integrity, yet in return met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal to the end, he met calamity.

sentences.zh: 小弁之作，離騷之興，皆由此也。

translations.literal: The making of "Little Boy" and the rise of "Encountering Sorrow"—all sprang from this.
translations.idiomatic: Such wrongs bred the laments of Little Boy and Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 就或佞邪，盜言孔甘，猶當清覽，憎而知善；

translations.literal: Suppose some are fawning and wicked, stolen words so sweet—still one ought to clear-sightedly read them, hate yet know the good;
translations.idiomatic: Even sweet slander should be read with cool judgment;

sentences.zh: 讒巧似直，惑亂聖聽，尚望文告，使知所由。

translations.literal: slander clever seeming straight, confusing and disordering sage hearing—still I hope for written proclamation, letting us know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: we beg a written charge so we may know the crime.

sentences.zh: 若信有罪，當垂三宥；

translations.literal: If indeed there is guilt, you ought to extend the three pardons;
translations.idiomatic: If he sinned, apply the thrice-repeated mercy;

sentences.zh: 若不改寤，計功減降，當在八議。

translations.literal: if he does not wake and repent, reckon merit and reduce rank—he should fall within the eight deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: if not, weigh merit under the eight grounds of clemency.

sentences.zh: 而潛軍伺襲，大兵奄至，舞戈長驅，衝擊遼土。

translations.literal: Yet hidden troops watched and raided, great hosts suddenly arrived, brandishing spears in long drive, charging Liaodong soil.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you sent secret armies to storm the northeast.

sentences.zh: 犬馬惡死，況於人類！

translations.literal: Dogs and horses hate death—how much more mankind!
translations.idiomatic: Even beasts cling to life—what of men?

sentences.zh: 吏民昧死，挫辱王師。

translations.literal: Officials and people risked death, blocked and insulted the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Our people met your host with desperate resistance.

sentences.zh: 淵雖冤枉，方臨危殆，猶恃聖恩，悵然重奔，冀必奸臣矯制，妄肆威虐，乃謂臣等曰：『漢安帝建光元年，遼東屬國都尉龐奮，受三月乙未詔書，曰收幽州刺史馮煥、玄菟太守姚光。

translations.literal: Although Yuan was wronged, as he faced peril he still relied on sage grace, sadly turned again in flight, surely thinking some wicked minister had forged the edict and wantonly wielded cruelty; thereupon he said to us and others: "In Han Andi's Jianguang first year, the colonel of the dependent state of Liaodong, Pang Fen, received a third-month yimao day edict saying to arrest Governor of Youzhou Feng Huan and Governor of Xuantu Yao Guang.
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis Yuan still trusted the throne, telling us: "In 121 the Liaodong colonel Pang Fen got a forged edict to seize Youzhou and Xuantu governors—

sentences.zh: 推案無乙未詔書，遣侍御史幽州

translations.literal: They pushed the case and found no yimao edict, dispatched palace attendant censor to Youzhou
translations.idiomatic: investigation showed no such order; the court sent a censor to Youzhou

translations.literal: (The text supplies the graph for governor.)
translations.idiomatic: (The manuscript adds the title "governor.")

sentences.zh: 考奸臣矯制者。

translations.literal: to examine who had forged the edict.
translations.idiomatic: To hunt the forger.

sentences.zh: 今刺史或儻謬承矯制乎？

translations.literal: Now has the governor perhaps wrongly accepted a forged order?"
translations.idiomatic: Has our governor mistaken another forgery for law?"

sentences.zh: 』臣等議：以為刺史興兵，搖動天下，殆非矯制，必是詔命。

translations.literal: 」We deliberated: we thought that for a governor to raise troops and shake the empire is hardly a forgery—it must be a true edict.
translations.idiomatic: We answered: a provincial war on this scale must be imperial command, not a fake."

sentences.zh: 淵乃俯仰嘆息，自傷無罪。

translations.literal: Yuan thereupon looked up and down, sighed, and wounded himself over having no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sighed his innocence.

sentences.zh: 深惟土地所以養人，竊慕古公杖策之岐，乃欲投冠釋紱，逝歸林麓。

translations.literal: Deeply he thought that land exists to nurture people; privately he admired the ancient duke who leaned on his staff to Qi, therefore wished to cast off cap and unbind sash and depart to forest and foothill.
translations.idiomatic: He thought of fleeing to the hills like the ancient lord who left Bin for Qi.

sentences.zh: 臣等維持，誓之以死，屯守府門，不聽所執。

translations.literal: We and others held him fast, swore with death, encamped guarding the prefecture gate, would not listen to what he grasped.
translations.idiomatic: We swore to die blocking his gate.

sentences.zh: 而七營虎士，五部蠻夷，各懷素飽，不謀同心，奮臂大呼，排門遁出。

translations.literal: Yet the seven camps of tiger warriors, the five divisions of Man and Yi, each with a full belly from long rations, without plotting shared one heart, raised arms with great shouts, pushed the gate and burst out.
translations.idiomatic: Seven tiger camps and tribal auxiliaries, well fed and of one mind, smashed the gates to fight.

sentences.zh: 近郊農民，釋其耨鎛，伐薪制梃，改案為櫓，奔馳赴難，軍旅行成，雖蹈湯火，死不顧生。

translations.literal: Near-suburb farmers put aside hoe and mattock, cut fuel and made clubs, changed harrow for shield, galloped to the crisis; the army's line formed in a trice—though they trod soup and fire, they did not look to save their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers grabbed clubs and shields and ran to battle as if into boiling oil.

sentences.zh: 淵雖見孤棄，怨而不怒，比遣敕軍，勿得乾犯，及手書告語，懇惻至誠。

translations.literal: Although Yuan saw himself orphaned and cast aside, he resented but did not rage; repeatedly he sent orders to the army not to commit violations, and by his own hand wrote letters of notice, earnest and utmost sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forbade his men to harm imperial troops and wrote pleading letters in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 而吏士凶悍，不可解散，期於畢命，投死無悔。

translations.literal: Yet officers and soldiers were fierce and violent, could not be dispersed, fixed on exhausting their lives, threw themselves to death without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers would not stand down—they meant to fight to the last.

sentences.zh: 淵懼吏士不從教令，乃躬馳騖，自往化解，僅乃止之。

translations.literal: Yuan feared officers and soldiers would not obey teaching orders; thereupon himself galloped back and forth, personally went to dissolve it, barely then stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: He rode among them himself and barely checked the rush.

sentences.zh: 一飯之惠，匹夫所死，況淵累葉信結百姓，恩著民心。

translations.literal: The grace of one meal, a common man dies for it—how much more Yuan, whose many generations bound trust with the hundred surnames, whose grace showed in the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: A single meal wins a commoner's death—how much more generations of kindness to Liaodong?

sentences.zh: 自先帝初興，爰暨陛下，榮淵累葉，豐功懿德，策名褒揚，辯著廊廟，勝衣舉履，誦詠明文，以為口實。

translations.literal: From the time the late founding emperor first rose down to your Majesty, glory to Yuan's many generations, abundant merit and fine virtue, inscribing the name in praise, clear in hall and temple—those who can don coat and lift shoe recite the bright text and take it as talk on the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Cao's rise to your reign the Gongsuns' deeds have been sung in court and market.

sentences.zh: 埋而掘之，古人所恥。

translations.literal: To bury and then dig up—this the ancients shamed.
translations.idiomatic: To honor a man then destroy him shames any king who reads history.

sentences.zh: 小白、重耳，衰世諸侯，猶慕著信，以隆霸業。

translations.literal: Little White and Chong'er, declining-age feudal lords, still admired manifest trust to raise hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Even Duke Huan and Wen of Jin built hegemony on faith.

sentences.zh: 詩美文王作孚萬邦，論語稱仲尼去食存信；

translations.literal: The Odes praise King Wen for making trust in myriad states; the Analects says Confucius would leave food but preserve trust;
translations.idiomatic: The Songs praise King Wen's good faith; the Analects say the Master would starve before breaking trust;

sentences.zh: 信之為德，固亦大矣。

translations.literal: trust as virtue is indeed also great.
translations.idiomatic: for faith is the greatest virtue.

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀共帝，鼎足而居，天下搖盪，無所統一，臣等每為陛下懼此危心。

translations.literal: Now Wu and Shu together style themselves emperors, stand like tripod legs, the empire shakes and has no unity—we your subjects each for your Majesty fear this peril in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu now rival the throne while the realm totters—we tremble for you.

sentences.zh: 淵據金城之固，仗和睦之民，國殷兵強，可以橫行。

translations.literal: Yuan relied on metal-walled firmness, leaned on harmonious people, state rich and army strong—he could have ranged at will.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan held a strong land and loyal people—he could have been your shield.

sentences.zh: 策名委質，守死善道，忠至義盡，為九州表。

translations.literal: Inscribing the name and pledging substance, guarding death and good way, loyalty reached and righteousness exhausted—he was a model for the nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged life to lawful duty—a model to the nine regions.

sentences.zh: 方今二敵闚𨵦，未知孰定，是之不戒，而淵是害。

translations.literal: Just now the two foes peer from their corners; we do not know which will prevail—this you do not guard against, yet harm comes to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: You eye two enemies yet strike the loyal bulwark first.

sentences.zh: 茹柔吐剛，非王者之道也。

translations.literal: To chew the soft and spit the hard is not the way of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Swallowing the meek and spitting the tough is no way to rule.

sentences.zh: 臣等雖鄙，誠竊恥之。

translations.literal: We your subjects although mean, truly privately are shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: We are humble men, yet we blush for this policy.

sentences.zh: 若無天乎，臣一郡吉凶，尚未可知；

translations.literal: If there is no Heaven, then our one commandery's weal and woe is still not yet to be known;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven does not watch, our fate is dark;

sentences.zh: 若云有天，亦何懼焉！

translations.literal: if one says there is Heaven, what then is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven watches, why should we fear to speak truth!

sentences.zh: 臣等聞仕於家者，二世則主之，三世則君之。

translations.literal: We your subjects have heard that one who serves a house, at the second generation serves him as lord, at the third generation serves him as prince.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard: two generations serve as house; the third owes liege duty.

sentences.zh: 臣等生於荒裔之土，出於圭竇之中，無大援於魏，世隸於公孫氏，報生與賜，在於死力。

translations.literal: We your subjects were born in wild border soil, came out of hovels in the wall, had no great support from Wei, generation after generation were bound to the Gongsun house—repaying life and bounty lies in deadly effort.
translations.idiomatic: We are border folk bound to the Gongsuns for generations—we owe them our lives.

sentences.zh: 昔蒯通言直，漢祖赦其誅；

translations.literal: Formerly Kuai Tong spoke straight and Han Gaozu pardoned his execution;
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong's blunt counsel won pardon from Han Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 鄭詹辭順，晉文原其死。

translations.literal: Zhan's words were compliant and Jin Wen forgave his death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's soft plea moved Jin Wen to spare him.

sentences.zh: 臣等頑愚，不達大節，苟執一介，披露肝膽，言逆龍鱗，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: We your subjects are stubborn and foolish, do not reach great integrity, but if we hold one conviction, lay bare liver and gall, words offend dragon scales, crime should be ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: We are fools, yet we bare our hearts though it cost ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下恢崇撫育，亮其控告，使疏遠之臣，永有保持。

translations.literal: Only may your Majesty enlarge cherishing and nurture, brighten their plaint and charge, letting distant ministers forever have preservation and holding.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you widen mercy and shelter those who speak from afar.

sentences.zh: 初，淵家數有怪，犬冠幘絳衣上屋，炊有小兒蒸死甑中。

translations.literal: At first in Yuan's household several times there were prodigies: a dog capped and in crimson climbed the roof; in the steamer a small child was steamed dead.
translations.idiomatic: Strange signs plagued Yuan's house—a capped dog on the roof, a child found steamed in the pot.

sentences.zh: 襄平北巿生肉，長圍各數尺，有頭目口喙，無手足而動搖。

translations.literal: In the north market of Xiangping flesh was born, lengths several feet each around, having head, eyes, mouth, and beak, without hands or feet yet swaying.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh grew in Xiangping market with eyes and beak yet no limbs, twitching alive.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有形不成，有體無聲，其國滅亡。

translations.literal: The divination said: "Having form but not completing, having body without sound—its state will perish and be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Form without completion, body without sound—the state will fall."

sentences.zh: 」始度以中平六年據遼東，至淵三世，凡五十年而滅。

translations.literal: 」At first Du in the sixth year of Zhongping took Liaodong; down to Yuan three generations—altogether fifty years—and was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: 」Du seized Liaodong in 189; three generations and fifty years later the line ended.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：始淵兄晃為恭任子，在洛，聞淵劫奪恭位，謂淵終不可保，數自表聞，欲令國家討淵。

translations.literal: 〈The Weilüe says: At first Yuan's elder brother Huang was hostage for Gong at Luoyang; hearing Yuan coerced and seized Gong's position, he said Yuan in the end could not be preserved, repeatedly himself memorialized, wishing the state to punish Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe: Yuan Huang was hostage in Luoyang; learning of the coup he begged Wei to strike his brother.

sentences.zh: 帝以淵已秉權，故因而撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor because Yuan already held power, therefore went along and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared Huang because Yuan already held the northeast.

sentences.zh: 及淵叛，遂以國法系晃。

translations.literal: When Yuan rebelled, thereupon by the laws of the state bound Huang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan rebelled, Huang was seized by law.

sentences.zh: 晃雖有前言，冀不坐，然內以骨肉，知淵破則己從及。

translations.literal: Although Huang had earlier words, he hoped not to sit for crime, yet inwardly as bone and flesh he knew when Yuan fell he himself would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Huang hoped his warnings would save him, yet knew he would share the fall.

sentences.zh: 淵首到，晃自審必死，與其子相對啼哭。

translations.literal: When Yuan's head arrived, Huang examined himself and was sure to die, with his son faced each other weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan's head came west, Huang knew he was doomed and wept with his son.

sentences.zh: 時上亦欲活之，而有司以為不可，遂殺之。〉

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign also wished to let him live, but the responsible offices held it could not be done, thereupon killed him.〉
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to spare him; the law officers refused—so Huang died.〉

sentences.zh: 張繡，武威祖厲人，驃騎將軍濟族子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu was a man of Zuli in Wuwei, a nephew of the general of agile cavalry Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu of Zuli in Wuwei was a kinsman of Zhang Ji the general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 邊章、韓遂為亂涼州，金城麴勝襲殺祖厲長劉雋。

translations.literal: When Bian Zhang and Han Sui made rebellion in Liangzhou, Qu Sheng of Jincheng raided and killed the magistrate of Zuli, Liu Juan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou rose, Qu Sheng of Jincheng murdered Magistrate Liu Juan of Zuli.

sentences.zh: 繡為縣吏，間伺殺勝，郡內義之。

translations.literal: Xiu was a county clerk; he spied an opening and killed Sheng; the commandery deemed him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Xiu avenged him by killing Qu Sheng and won local praise.

sentences.zh: 遂招合少年，為邑中豪傑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered and joined young men and became a stalwart of the town.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied town youths and became a local power.

sentences.zh: 董卓敗，濟與李傕等擊呂布，為卓報仇。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo was defeated, Ji with Li Jue and others struck Lü Bu to avenge Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo fell, Ji joined Li Jue against Lü Bu to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 語在

translations.literal: The language is in
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in

sentences.zh: 〈卓傳〉

translations.literal: 〈the biography of Zhuo〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhuo's biography〉
(end of cross-reference).

sentences.zh: 繡隨濟，以軍功稍遷至建忠將軍，封宣威侯。

translations.literal: Xiu followed Ji; by military merit he gradually rose to general who establishes loyalty and was enfeoffed marquis of Xuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu followed Ji, won rank on merit, became general who establishes loyalty, and marquis of Xuanwei.

sentences.zh: 濟屯弘農，士卒飢餓，南攻穰，為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: Ji garrisoned Hongnong; soldiers starved; he attacked south toward Rang and was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ji camped at Hongnong, starved his men, marched on Rang, and fell to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 繡領其眾，屯宛，與劉表合。

translations.literal: Xiu led his host, garrisoned Wan, and joined with Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu took the command, held Wan, and allied with Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 太祖南征，軍淯水，繡等舉眾降。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned south; the army was at Yu water; Xiu and others raised the host and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched south to the Yu River; Xiu brought the whole force over.

sentences.zh: 太祖納濟妻，繡恨之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor took Ji's wife in marriage; Xiu resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took Zhang Ji's widow—Xiu burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其不悅，密有殺繡之計。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard he was not pleased and secretly had a plan to kill Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heard of his spleen and plotted his murder.

sentences.zh: 計漏，繡掩襲太祖。

translations.literal: The plan leaked; Xiu surprise-attacked the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Word slipped out; Xiu struck first.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍敗，二子沒。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's army was defeated; two sons perished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao lost the field and two sons.

sentences.zh: 繡還保穰，

translations.literal: Xiu returned to defend Rang,
translations.idiomatic: Xiu withdrew to Rang,

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：繡有所親胡車兒，勇冠其軍。

translations.literal: 〈the Fuzi says: Xiu had a favored Hu named Che Er, bravest in his army.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Fuzi: Xiu's favorite Hu warrior Che Er was the bravest man in camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖愛其驍健，手以金與之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor loved his fierceness and strength and with his own hand gave him gold.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao admired his dash and handed him gold with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 繡聞而疑太祖欲因左右刺之，遂反。

translations.literal: Xiu heard and suspected the Grand Progenitor wished through those at his side to stab him; thereupon he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu thought the gold was a bribe to assassinate him and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：繡降，

translations.literal: The Wushu says: When Xiu surrendered,
translations.idiomatic: The Wushu adds: when Xiu first yielded,

sentences.zh: （凌統）

translations.literal: (The manuscript gloss reads Ling Tong.)
translations.idiomatic: (Marginal gloss: Ling Tong.)

sentences.zh: 用賈詡計，乞徙軍就高道，道由太祖屯中。

translations.literal: Using Jia Xu's plan, he begged to move the army onto the high road, the route passing through the Grand Progenitor's encampment.
translations.idiomatic: At Jia Xu's suggestion he asked to redeploy along the heights through Cao Cao's camp.

sentences.zh: 繡又曰：「車少而重，乞得使兵各被甲。

translations.literal: Xiu again said: "The carts are few and heavy; I beg to have the soldiers each don armor."
translations.idiomatic: He added that the wagons were heavy and every man should wear mail.

sentences.zh: 」太祖信繡，皆聽之。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Progenitor trusted Xiu and granted everything.
translations.idiomatic: 」Cao Cao trusted him and agreed.

sentences.zh: 繡乃嚴兵入屯，掩太祖。

translations.literal: Xiu then with strict troops entered the garrison and surprise-attacked the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: He marched armed men in and struck by surprise.

sentences.zh: 太祖不備，故敗。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was unprepared, therefore was defeated.〉
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was caught flat-footed and lost.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖比年攻之，不克。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor for successive years attacked him but could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao besieged him for years without success.

sentences.zh: 太祖拒袁紹於官渡，繡從賈詡計，復以眾降。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor resisted Yuan Shao at Guandu, Xiu followed Jia Xu's plan and again with the host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu he followed Jia Xu and brought his army over again.

sentences.zh: 語在

translations.literal: The language is in
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in

sentences.zh: 〈詡傳〉

translations.literal: 〈the biography of Xu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jia Xu's biography〉
(end of cross-reference).

sentences.zh: 繡至，太祖執其手，與歡宴，為子均取繡女，拜揚武將軍。

translations.literal: When Xiu arrived, the Grand Progenitor grasped his hand, feasted with him in joy, for his son Jun took Xiu's daughter in marriage, and appointed him general who displays martial might.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao clasped his hand, feasted him, married his son Jun to Xiu's daughter, and named him general who displays martial might.

sentences.zh: 官渡之役，繡力戰有功，遷破羌將軍。

translations.literal: In the Guandu campaign Xiu fought hard with merit and was promoted general who breaks the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Guandu he fought fiercely and rose to general who breaks the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 從破袁譚於南皮，復增邑凡二千戶。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Yuan Tan at Nanpi; his fief was again enlarged to two thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the storming of Nanpi and gained two thousand households in total fief.

sentences.zh: 是時天下戶口減耗，十裁一在，諸將封未有滿千戶者，而繡特多。

translations.literal: At this time household registers under heaven had shrunk; perhaps one in ten remained; of the generals' enfeoffments none had reached a thousand households, yet Xiu was exceptionally many.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm depopulated, few generals held a thousand-house fief—Xiu stood out.

sentences.zh: 從征烏丸於柳城，未至，薨，諡曰定侯。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Wuhuan at Liucheng; before reaching, he passed away; posthumous title was settled marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the march to Liucheng against the Wuhuan and received the posthumous title settled marquis.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：五官將數因請會，發怒曰：「君殺吾​​兄，何忍持面視人邪！

translations.literal: 〈The Weilüe says: The heir apparent of the five offices several times used the occasion of a requested gathering to flare in anger, saying: "You killed my elder brother—how can you bear to show your face to others!"
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Weilüe: Cao Pi repeatedly snarled at feasts, "You killed my brother—how dare you show your face?"

sentences.zh: 」繡心不自安，乃自殺。〉

translations.literal: 」Xiu's heart was not at peace; thereupon he killed himself.〉
translations.idiomatic: 」Xiu could not live with the shame and took his own life.〉

sentences.zh: 子泉嗣，坐與魏諷謀反誅，國除。

translations.literal: His son Quan succeeded; because he sat in conspiracy with Wei Feng to rebel, he was executed and the state removed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan inherited the title, joined Wei Feng's plot, died for it, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 張魯字公祺，沛國豐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu, courtesy name Gongqi, was a man of Feng in the state of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu, courtesy Gongqi, came from Feng in Pei.

sentences.zh: 祖父陵，客蜀，學道鵠鳴山中，造作道書以惑百姓，從受道者出五斗米，故世號米賊。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ling, a guest in Shu, studied the Way on Mount Heming, forged Daoist writings to delude the hundred surnames; those who received the Way from him paid out five pecks of rice, therefore the age called them the rice bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ling settled in Shu, preached on Mount Heming, forged scriptures, and charged five pecks of rice per initiate—hence "Five Pecks of Rice" sect.

sentences.zh: 陵死，子衡行其道。

translations.literal: When Ling died, his son Heng practiced his Way.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's son Heng continued the teaching.

sentences.zh: 衡死，魯復行之。

translations.literal: When Heng died, Lu again practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng died, Lu inherited the movement.

sentences.zh: 益州牧劉焉以魯為督義司馬，與別部司馬張脩將兵擊漢中太守蘇固，魯遂襲脩殺之，奪其眾。

translations.literal: Shepherd of Yizhou Liu Yan made Lu colonel who supervises righteousness, and with colonel of a separate division Zhang Xiu led troops to strike the governor of Hanzhong Su Gu; Lu thereupon raided Xiu, killed him, and seized his host.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan named Lu colonel who supervises righteousness; Lu marched with Zhang Xiu against Hanzhong governor Su Gu, then murdered Xiu and swallowed his troops.

sentences.zh: 焉死，子璋代立，以魯不順，盡殺魯母家室。

translations.literal: When Yan died, his son Zhang succeeded; because Lu was not obedient, he killed all of Lu's mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang killed Lu's kin when Lu defied him.

sentences.zh: 魯遂據漢中，以鬼道教民，自號「師君」。

translations.literal: Lu thereupon occupied Hanzhong, used ghost doctrine to teach the people, and styled himself "lord master."
translations.idiomatic: Lu seized Hanzhung, ruled by spirit cult, and called himself lord master.

sentences.zh: 其來學道者，初皆名「鬼卒」。

translations.literal: Those who first came to study the Way were all named "ghost privates."
translations.idiomatic: New initiates were titled ghost privates.

sentences.zh: 受本道已信，號「祭酒」。

translations.literal: When they had received the root teaching and were trusted, they were titled "libationer."
translations.idiomatic: Trusted adepts became libationers.

sentences.zh: 各領部眾，多者為治頭大祭酒。

translations.literal: Each led a following; the one with many was chief libationer of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Each led a congregation; the largest bands had chief libationers.

sentences.zh: 皆教以誠信不欺詐，有病自首其過，大都與黃巾相似。

translations.literal: All were taught sincerity and faith without fraud; if sick they confessed their faults—largely similar to the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: He preached honesty, confession of sin for illness—much like the Yellow Turbans.

sentences.zh: 諸祭酒皆作義舍，如今之亭傳。

translations.literal: The libationers all built righteousness lodges, like today's post stations.
translations.idiomatic: Libationers built hostels like government relay inns.

sentences.zh: 又置義米肉，縣於義舍，行路者量腹取足；

translations.literal: Again they set out righteousness rice and meat, hung them in the righteousness lodges; travelers measured belly and took enough;
translations.idiomatic: They hung rice and meat in the lodges for wayfarers to take as needed;

sentences.zh: 若過多，鬼道輒病之。

translations.literal: if they took too much, the ghost way then afflicted them.
translations.idiomatic: greed brought supernatural illness.

sentences.zh: 犯法者，三原，然後乃行刑。

translations.literal: For lawbreakers, three pardons, and only then was punishment applied.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders were forgiven thrice before punishment.

sentences.zh: 不置長吏，皆以祭酒為治，民夷便樂之。

translations.literal: They did not appoint chief clerks; all used libationers for government; the people and Yi were pleased with it.
translations.idiomatic: Libationers replaced magistrates; Han and tribal folk accepted the rule.

sentences.zh: 雄據巴、漢垂三十年。

translations.literal: He powerfully held Ba and Han for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He dominated Ba and Hanzhong for almost thirty years.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：熹平中，妖賊大起，三輔有駱曜。

translations.literal: 〈The Dianlüe says: In the Xiping era demon bandits rose greatly; in the three adjuncts there was Luo Yao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Dianlüe: in the 170s rebels swelled in the capital region, including Luo Yao.

sentences.zh: 光和中，東方有張角，漢中有張脩。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era, in the east there was Zhang Jue; in Hanzhong there was Zhang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghe years Zhang Jue rose in the east and Zhang Xiu in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 駱曜教民緬匿法，角為太平道，脩為五斗米道。

translations.literal: Luo Yao taught the people the hiding-by-bending method; Jue had the Way of Great Peace; Xiu had the Way of Five Pecks of Rice.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yao taught concealment; Jue preached Great Peace; Xiu the Five Pecks of Rice.

sentences.zh: 太平道者，師持九節杖為符祝，教病人叩頭思過，因以符水飲之，得病或日淺而癒者，則云此人信道，其或不愈，則為不信道。

translations.literal: As for the Way of Great Peace, the master held a nine-jointed staff as talisman and prayer, taught the sick to knock their heads and think on faults, then by means of talisman water made them drink it; if the illness was shallow and they recovered in a day, then it was said this person believed the Way; if they did not recover, then it was said they did not believe the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Great Peace healers used nine-knot staves, confession, and charmed water—cure proved faith, lingering illness proved doubt.

sentences.zh: 脩法略與角同，加施靜室，使病者處其中思過。

translations.literal: Xiu's method was roughly the same as Jue's, adding the application of quiet chambers, making the sick dwell within them and think on faults.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu added silent cells where the sick meditated on sin.

sentences.zh: 又使人為奸令祭酒，祭酒主以老子五千文，使都習，號為奸令。

translations.literal: Again he made men libationers of wicked orders; the libationers took charge of the Laozi in five thousand words, made all study it, and styled it wicked order.
translations.idiomatic: He named "wicked-order" libationers to drill the Daodejing into followers.

sentences.zh: 為鬼吏，主為病者請禱。

translations.literal: As ghost clerks they took charge of praying for the sick.
translations.idiomatic: Ghost clerks led prayer for the ill.

sentences.zh: 請禱之法，書病人姓名，說服罪之意。

translations.literal: The method of requesting prayer: write the sick person's name, state the meaning of confessing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote the patient's name and confession of guilt.

sentences.zh: 作三通，其一上之天，著山上，其一埋之地，其一沉之水，謂之三官手書。

translations.literal: They made three copies: one went up to Heaven and was placed on the mountain; one was buried in earth; one was sunk in water—called the three-officers hand document.
translations.idiomatic: Three copies went to heaven, earth, and water—the "three officers" writ.

sentences.zh: 使病者家出米五斗以為常，故號曰五斗米師。

translations.literal: They made the sick person's household pay five pecks of rice as regular rule, therefore the title was master of five pecks of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Each family paid five pecks of rice in fees—hence the sect name.

sentences.zh: 實無益於治病，但為淫妄，然小人昏愚，競共事之。

translations.literal: In truth it did not benefit curing illness, only was wanton delusion, yet petty men, dim and foolish, vied to serve it.
translations.idiomatic: It cured nothing but duped the credulous.

sentences.zh: 後角被誅，脩亦亡。

translations.literal: Later Jue was executed; Xiu also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was executed; Xiu died too.

sentences.zh: 及魯在漢中，因其民信行脩業，遂增飾之。

translations.literal: When Lu was in Hanzhong, because the people believed and practiced Xiu's enterprise, he thereupon enlarged and embellished it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu expanded Xiu's practices once he held Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 教使作義舍，以米肉置其中以止行人；

translations.literal: He taught them to make righteousness lodges and place rice and meat inside to stop travelers;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered righteousness lodges stocked with food for travelers;

sentences.zh: 又教使自隱，有小過者，當治道百步，則罪除；

translations.literal: Again he taught them to conceal themselves; for those with small faults, they should repair a hundred paces of road, then guilt was removed;
translations.idiomatic: Minor sinners paved a hundred paces of road to atone;

sentences.zh: 又依月令，春夏禁殺；

translations.literal: again according to monthly ordinances, in spring and summer killing was forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: spring and summer brought a ban on slaughter;

sentences.zh: 又禁酒。

translations.literal: again wine was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: wine was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 流移寄在其地者，不敢不奉。

translations.literal: Drifters who lodged in that land did not dare not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees dared not defy these rules.

sentences.zh: 臣松之謂：張脩應是張衡，非《典略》之失，則傳寫之誤。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: Zhang Xiu ought to be Zhang Heng; if it is not the Dianlüe's error, then it is a scribal error in transmission.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: Xiu here is likely Zhang Heng—a slip in the Dianlüe or copyists.〉

sentences.zh: 漢末，力不能征，遂就寵魯為鎮民中郎將，領漢寧太守，通貢獻而已。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, strength could not campaign; thereupon they drew near and enfeoffed Lu as colonel who pacifies the people among the gentlemen of the household, leading governor of Hanning, communicating tribute only.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han could not crush him and instead enfeoffed him as pacifying colonel and governor of Hanning while he merely sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 民有地中得玉印者，群下欲尊魯為漢寧王。

translations.literal: When the people had one who obtained a jade seal in the ground, the host of subordinates wished to honor Lu as king of Hanning.
translations.idiomatic: A peasant found a jade seal; his aides urged Lu to take the title king of Hanning.

sentences.zh: 魯功曹巴西閻圃諫魯曰：「漢川之民，戶出十萬，財富土沃，四面險固；

translations.literal: Lu's merit clerk Yan Pu of Ba admonished Lu, saying: "The people of the Han river lands, households numbering a hundred thousand, wealth abundant, soil fertile, four sides perilously firm;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pu urged restraint: "You command a hundred thousand households on rich soil behind natural walls;

sentences.zh: 上匡天子，則為桓、文，次及竇融，不失富貴。

translations.literal: if above you aid the Son of Heaven, then you are Huan and Wen; next you are Dou Rong—not losing wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: serve the emperor as a hegemon or as Dou Rong did and keep wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 今承製署置，勢足斬斷，不煩於王。

translations.literal: Now if you undertake interim appointments, your power is enough to cut off rivals—you need not trouble with kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Interim titles already give you power—do not rush the crown.

sentences.zh: 原且不稱，勿為禍先。

translations.literal: I pray you for the moment not to assume it; do not be the first to invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wait—do not court ruin."

sentences.zh: 」魯從之。

translations.literal: 」Lu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Lu listened.

sentences.zh: 韓遂、馬超之亂，關西民從子午谷奔之者數万家。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Han Sui and Ma Chao, ten thousand households of people west of the pass fled to him through the Ziwu valley.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui and Ma Chao rose, tens of thousands fled west-of-pass folk to him via Ziwu Gorge.

sentences.zh: 建安二十年，太祖乃自散關出武都征之，至陽平關。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jian'an, the Grand Progenitor thereupon himself came out from Sanguan through Wudu to campaign against him, reaching Yangping pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 20 (215) Cao Cao marched from Sanguan through Wudu to Yangping.

sentences.zh: 魯欲舉漢中降，其弟衛不肯，率眾數万人拒關堅守。

translations.literal: Lu wished to raise Hanzhong and surrender; his younger brother Wei would not, led a host of several tens of thousands to block the pass and firmly guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lu wished to yield; his brother Wei refused and held the pass with tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻破之，遂入蜀。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor broke him, thereupon entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao stormed the pass and drove into Shu.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏名臣奏》載董昭表曰：

translations.literal: 〈The Wei mingchen zou carries Dong Zhao's memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Dong Zhao's memorial in Wei mingchen zou states:

sentences.zh: 武皇帝承涼州從事及武都降人之辭，說張魯易攻，陽平城下南北山相遠，不可守也，信以為然。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor took the words of a Liangzhou clerk and surrendered men from Wudu, saying Zhang Lu was easy to attack, that south and north mountains at Yangping city were far apart and could not be defended—he believed it true.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao believed Liangzhou clerks who said Yangping was weakly held.

sentences.zh: 及往臨履，不如所聞，乃歎曰：『他人商度，少如人意。

translations.literal: When he went and trod the ground, it was not as heard; he then sighed, saying: "Others' reckonings seldom match human intent."
translations.idiomatic: On the ground he found otherwise and sighed that others' maps lie.

sentences.zh: 』攻陽平山上諸屯，既不時拔，士卒傷夷者多。

translations.literal: 」Attacking the various garrisons on Yangping mountain, they could not be taken in good time; many soldiers were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain forts resisted; casualties mounted.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝意沮，便欲拔軍截山而還，遣故大將軍夏侯惇、將軍許褚呼山上兵還。

translations.literal: Martial Emperor's intent was dispirited; he then wished to pull up the army, cut the mountain, and return, dispatching former grand general Xiahou Dun and general Xu Chu to call back the mountain troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao planned retreat and ordered Xiahou Dun and Xu Chu to recall the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 會前軍未還，夜迷惑，誤入賊營，賊便退散。

translations.literal: It happened that the vanguard had not yet returned; in the night they were confused, mistakenly entered the bandit camp, and the bandits then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The night confused the lines—some troops blundered into Lu's camp and routed it by accident.

sentences.zh: 侍中辛毗、劉曄等在兵後，語惇、褚，言『官兵已據得賊要屯，賊已散走』。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Xin Pi, Liu Ye, and others were behind the troops and said to Dun and Chu that "the officers and soldiers have already seized the enemy's vital garrison; the bandits have scattered and fled."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi and Liu Ye behind the lines insisted the enemy was broken.

sentences.zh: 猶不信之。

translations.literal: Still they did not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Dun and Xu Chu doubted them.

sentences.zh: 惇前自見，乃還白武皇帝，進兵定之，幸而克獲。

translations.literal: Dun went forward and saw for himself, then returned and reported to Martial Emperor; he advanced troops and settled it, fortunately then capturing victory.
translations.idiomatic: Dun rode up, saw the truth, and Cao Cao pressed on to victory.

sentences.zh: 此近事，吏士所知。

translations.literal: This is recent affair, known to clerks and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Living officers still remember it.

sentences.zh: 又楊暨表曰：

translations.literal: Again Yang Ji submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji also memorialized:

sentences.zh: 武皇帝始征張魯，以十萬之眾，身親臨履，指授方略，因就民麥以為軍糧。

translations.literal: When Martial Emperor first campaigned against Zhang Lu, with a host of one hundred thousand, he personally trod the ground, pointed and instructed strategy, and thereby took the people's wheat for army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao led a hundred thousand men, requisitioned wheat, and laid his own plans.

sentences.zh: 張衛之守，蓋不足言。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei's defense is hardly worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei's defense was nothing special.

sentences.zh: 地險守易，雖有精兵虎將，勢不能施。

translations.literal: The ground perilous, defense easy—although there were crack troops and tiger generals, the situation could not be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Terrain favored the defender—elite troops could not deploy.

sentences.zh: 對兵三日，欲抽軍還，言『作軍三十年，一朝持與人，如何』。

translations.literal: Facing battle three days, he wished to draw the army back, saying: "Thirty years making armies—in one morning handing them to the enemy—how can that be?"
translations.idiomatic: After three days he talked of quitting—"thirty years building an army, lost in a day."

sentences.zh: 此計已定，天祚大魏，魯守自壞，因以定之。

translations.literal: This plan was already fixed; Heaven aided great Wei—Lu's defense collapsed of itself, and thereby it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He had chosen retreat when Heaven broke Lu's line for him.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：魯遣五官掾降，弟衛橫山築陽平城以拒，王師不得進。

translations.literal: The Shiyu says: Lu sent his aide of the five offices to surrender; his younger brother Wei built Yangping city athwart the mountain to resist, and the royal army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu: Lu offered surrender while Wei walled Yangping and blocked the advance.

sentences.zh: 魯走巴中。

translations.literal: Lu fled to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Lu fled into Ba.

sentences.zh: 軍糧盡，太祖將還。

translations.literal: Army grain was exhausted; the Grand Progenitor was about to return.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies ran out; Cao Cao prepared to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 西曹掾東郡郭諶曰：「不可。

translations.literal: West-department aide Guo Chen of Dongjun said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chen objected: "We cannot leave.

sentences.zh: 魯已降，留使既未反，衛雖不同，偏攜可攻。

translations.literal: Lu has surrendered; the envoy left has not yet returned; although Wei disagrees, a partial strike can attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu has sued for peace; Wei alone holds out—hit him while he is isolated.

sentences.zh: 縣軍深入，以進必克，退必不免。

translations.literal: An army deep in enemy land—if we advance we must conquer; if we retreat we cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: We are deep in hostile ground—advance or die.

sentences.zh: 」太祖疑之。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Progenitor hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: 」Cao Cao wavered.

sentences.zh: 夜有野麋數千突壞衛營，軍大驚。

translations.literal: In the night several thousand wild elk burst and broke Wei's camp; the army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: That night a herd of elk stampeded Wei's camp.

sentences.zh: 夜，高祚等誤與衛眾遇，祚等多鳴鼓角會眾。

translations.literal: In the night Gao Zuo and others mistakenly encountered Wei's host; Zuo and others greatly beat drums and horns to gather the host.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zuo's scouts blundered into Wei, sounded drums, and panicked the defenders.

sentences.zh: 衛懼，以為大軍見掩，遂降。〉

translations.literal: Wei feared, thinking the great army had been masked against him, thereupon surrendered.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wei thought the main host had enveloped him and surrendered.〉

sentences.zh: 魯聞陽平已陷，將稽顙〔歸降〕，圃又曰：「今以迫往，功必輕；

translations.literal: When Lu heard Yangping had fallen, he was about to knock his forehead in submission; Pu again said: "If you go now under pressure, merit will surely be slight;
translations.idiomatic: When Yangping fell Yan Pu said, "Surrender now and your credit will be thin;

sentences.zh: 不如依

translations.literal: better to go to
translations.idiomatic: Better to take refuge with

sentences.zh: （杜灌）

translations.literal: (The manuscript reads Du Guan; the received text reads Du Hu.)
translations.idiomatic: (Textual variant: Du Guan versus Du Hu.)

sentences.zh: 〔杜濩〕赴樸胡相拒，然後委質，功必多。

translations.literal: Du Hu and join Pu Hu in resisting, then pledge allegiance—merit will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hu, join Pu Hu in resistance, then submit—you will earn far greater credit."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃奔南山入巴中。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he fled south into the mountains and entered Ba.
translations.idiomatic: 」So Lu fled south into Ba.

sentences.zh: 左右欲悉燒寶貨倉庫，魯曰：「本欲歸命國家，而意未達。

translations.literal: Those at his left and right wished to burn all treasure goods and storehouses; Lu said: "I originally wished to submit to the state, but my intent has not been reached.
translations.idiomatic: Aides urged burning the stores; Lu said, "I meant to yield to the court all along.

sentences.zh: 今之走，避銳鋒，非有惡意。

translations.literal: Now this flight is to avoid sharp points, not harboring evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: This retreat only dodges the spearhead, not treason.

sentences.zh: 寶貨倉庫，國家之有。

translations.literal: Treasure goods and storehouses belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Let the treasury fall to the state intact."

sentences.zh: 」遂封藏而去。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he sealed and stored them and left.
translations.idiomatic: 」He sealed the treasuries intact and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖入南鄭，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor entered Nan Zheng, he greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao entered Nan Zheng and praised his restraint.

sentences.zh: 又以魯本有善意，遣人慰喻。

translations.literal: Also because Lu originally had good intent, he sent men to console and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lu had meant well, Cao Cao sent envoys to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 魯盡將家出，太祖逆拜魯鎮南將軍，待以客禮，封閬中侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Lu brought his whole family out; the Grand Progenitor met him with a bow and appointed Lu general who guards the south, treated him with guest rites, enfeoffed him marquis of Langzhong, fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Lu came out with his kin; Cao Cao bowed, named him general who guards the south, treated him as an honored guest, and enfeoffed him marquis of Langzhong with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 封魯五子及閻圃等皆為列侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Lu's five sons and Yan Pu and others all as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's five sons and Yan Pu each received full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為張魯雖有善心，要為敗而後降，今乃寵以萬戶，五子皆封侯，過矣。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi considers: although Zhang Lu had good intent, in the essentials he surrendered only after defeat; now to favor him with ten thousand households and enfeoff all five sons as marquises is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi: Lu yielded only after defeat—such lavish rewards were excessive.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒曰：魯欲稱王，而閻圃諫止之，今封圃為列侯。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: Lu wished to style himself king, but Yan Pu remonstrated and stopped him; now he enfeoffs Pu as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi notes that Yan Pu stopped Lu from kingship—so ennobling Pu was fitting.

sentences.zh: 夫賞罰者，所以懲惡勸善也，苟其可以明軌訓於物，無遠近幽深矣。

translations.literal: As for rewards and punishments, they are the means to chastise evil and encourage good; if they can thereby make clear tracks and instruction for things, there is neither far nor near, deep nor hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments exist to deter evil and encourage good; used rightly they teach near and far alike.

sentences.zh: 今閻圃諫魯勿王，而太祖追封之，將來之人孰不思順！

translations.literal: Now Yan Pu remonstrated with Lu not to be king, yet the Grand Progenitor afterward enfeoffed him—which of men to come will not think to obey and yield!
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao honored Pu for that counsel, he taught the world to speak truth to power.

sentences.zh: 塞其本源而末流自止，其此之謂與！

translations.literal: Stop the source and the downstream currents stop of themselves—is it not this that is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Plug the headwaters and the flood abates—that is the point.

sentences.zh: 若乃不明於此而重燋爛之功，豐爵厚賞止於死戰之士，則民利於有亂，俗競於殺伐，阻兵仗力，干戈不戢矣。

translations.literal: If one is not clear on this yet stresses scorched-and-rotten merit, rich noble rank and thick reward stopping at men who died in battle, then the people will profit from having turmoil, custom will compete in killing and striking, block troops and rely on force, and spear and shield will not be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Reward only battlefield butchery and you teach the people to crave chaos and never sheathe arms.

sentences.zh: 太祖之此封，可謂知賞罰之本，雖湯武居之，無以加也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's enfeoffment here can be called knowing the root of rewards and punishments; though Tang and Wu held the throne, they could not add to it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's act grasped the root of justice—even Tang and Wu could not improve on it.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：黃初中，增圃爵邑，在禮請中。

translations.literal: The Weilüe says: In the Huangchu era Pu's noble rank and fief were increased; he lived out his days in honored retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The Weilüe adds that under Huangchu the court enlarged Yan Pu's fief and he ended his life in peace.

sentences.zh: 後十餘歲病死。

translations.literal: More than ten years later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness a decade later.

sentences.zh: 《晉書》云：西戎司馬閻纘，圃孫也。〉

translations.literal: The Jinshu says: Yan Zuan, western Rong marshal, was Pu's grandson.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshu names his grandson Yan Zuan, western Rong marshal.〉

sentences.zh: 為子彭祖取魯女。

translations.literal: He took a daughter of Lu for his son Pengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took Zhang Lu's daughter as wife for his son Pengzu.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：公孫瓚保京，坐待夷滅。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Gongsun Zan guarded Jing and sat waiting for extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: Gongsun Zan barricaded himself at Yi Jing and waited for ruin.

sentences.zh: 度殘暴而不節，淵仍業以載兇，秪足覆其族也。

translations.literal: Du was cruel and violent without restraint; Yuan inherited the enterprise and carried wickedness—only enough to overturn his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Du was savage; Yuan inherited his violence—both lines were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 陶謙昏亂而憂死，張楊授首於臣下，皆擁據州郡，曾匹夫之不若，固無可論者也。

translations.literal: Tao Qian was benighted and chaotic and died in worry; Zhang Yang lost his head to subordinates—all held commanderies and provinces yet were not the equal of a common man; solidly there is nothing worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian died in folly; Zhang Yang fell to his men—petty warlords beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 燕、繡、魯舍群盜，列功臣，去危亡，保宗祀，則於彼為愈焉。

translations.literal: Yan, Xiu, and Lu left the bandit hosts, ranked among meritorious ministers, escaped peril and death, and preserved ancestral sacrifice—there they did rather better.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, Zhang Xiu, and Zhang Lu quit banditry, joined the rolls of merit, saved their lines, and fared better than the rest.
